===== source_value_extractions table
CREATE TABLE "source_value_extractions" (
  extraction_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE HAND-OFF KEY (D-0168; pinned by the blocking judgment_handoff_shape check):
  -- NOT NULL, a real FK at the evidence item, and NO UNIQUE index over it anywhere.
  ref_id                 TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),

  -- The slug this extraction was mined under: HISTORY. No writer sets it after migration 114 (the scan
  -- contract, LED-195: a slug guides what is searched, not what is read from a source), so it is NULL on every
  -- later row. The admission record is source_slug_links.
  slug                   TEXT REFERENCES slugs(slug),

  -- THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26), now mandatory. Was nullable with `parameter` /
  -- `parameter_canonical` beside it; a NOT NULL free-text parameter NAME sitting next to
  -- a mandatory pointer at the registry that holds that same name is the dual home rule 5
  -- forbids. The name is reached: base_parameters.term_id -> terms.canonical_en.
  --
  -- AND THE VERBATIM PHRASE IS NOT LOST WITH IT. `parameter` was documented (schemas/
  -- source_value_extraction.py) as "the SOURCE's own phrase for what it measures,
  -- verbatim and unjudged (R11/D-0173)". That fact already has a purpose-built home with
  -- a live writer and 33 live rows: `observed_terms.surface_form`, whose own DDL comment
  -- reads "The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
  -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts" -- keyed
  -- UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language), with `locator` and `context_quote`, written
  -- by `db.py observe-term` and adjudicated by `adjudicate-term` (migration 068, D-0173).
  -- CLAUDE.md §6 orders exactly that split: "harvest concepts at evidence (db.py
  -- observe-term, verbatim and unjudged), adjudicate at judgment." `parameter` was the
  -- duplicate, and an UNREALISED one -- 0 rows, no writer, ever. Clause-level verbatim
  -- survives here in `claim_text` ("exact source phrasing") plus `source_section` and the
  -- 16 `loc_*` columns.
  --
  -- KNOWN RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: an extraction cannot say WHICH of
  -- its source's observations it was read from. Closing that is an `observation_id`
  -- pointer, and it is NOT added here because nothing would read it -- "an unread field,
  -- an uncalled script and an unregistered check are the same defect" (CLAUDE.md §8). Add
  -- it in the change that gives it a reader.
  parameter_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),

  -- THE FOUR LENSES (owner 2026-08-28; CHECK relaxed by D-0182). Real typed FKs, one per
  -- lens, nothing polymorphic. They replace `population_code` (retired by that ruling's
  -- own ACTION) and `population_label`, the free-text companion that had no registry at
  -- all -- retiring the typed column while keeping the untyped one beside it would keep
  -- the exact defect the ruling was issued against.
  --
  -- `base_taxonomy_medical` holds 0 rows today, so a NON-NULL medical_code is
  -- unwritable until it is seeded. That is the CLAUDE.md §4 trap, and it is harmless in
  -- this shape precisely because the column is nullable and the CHECK is "at least one":
  -- the table stays writable through any of the other three. `specifications` carries the
  -- identical arrangement from 071.
  identity_code          TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code),
  icf_code               TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
  needs_code             TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
  medical_code           TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),

  jurisdiction           TEXT,
  setting                TEXT,

  claim_type             TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (claim_type IN ('numerical','range','qualitative','framework','absent')),
  claimed_value          TEXT,
  claimed_unit           TEXT,
  claim_text             TEXT,
  source_section         TEXT,

  -- Value genealogy / independence substrate (DR-2026-07-13 H1), carried across
  -- unchanged. v_value_independence counts distinct roots over these.
  root_id                TEXT REFERENCES external_root_registry(root_id),   -- registry-only (R24); an in-corpus root is root_ref_id
  root_type              TEXT
                           CHECK (root_type IN (
                             'measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                             'committee_assertion', 'derived_calculation', 'untraced')),
  root_ref_id            TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
  echo_of                TEXT,
  measurement_paradigm   TEXT
                           CHECK (measurement_paradigm IN (
                             'swept_path_dynamic', 'static_turning_circle', 'static_clearance',
                             'anthropometric_percentile', 'instrumented_physical_measurement',
                             'route_metric', 'field_observation', 'participatory_spatial',
                             'stated_unmeasured')),
  device_class           TEXT
                           CHECK (device_class IN (
                             'manual_self_propelled', 'manual_attendant', 'power_chair', 'scooter',
                             'bariatric_manual', 'bariatric_power', 'walker_rollator',
                             'mixed', 'not_device_scoped')),
  root_population_note   TEXT,
  root_classification_basis TEXT,
  contested              INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
                           CHECK (contested IN (0, 1)),
  file_anchor            TEXT,

  -- Pinpoint locator hierarchy (migration 053), carried across unchanged. These are the
  -- clause-level address that makes D-0168's 1:N fan-out legible: NBC 3.8's many clauses
  -- are many rows, and these columns are what tells them apart.
  locator_scheme         TEXT,
  loc_division           TEXT,
  loc_part               TEXT,
  loc_section            TEXT,
  loc_subsection         TEXT,
  loc_paragraph          TEXT,
  loc_clause             TEXT,
  loc_subclause          TEXT,
  loc_division_end       TEXT,
  loc_part_end           TEXT,
  loc_section_end        TEXT,
  loc_subsection_end     TEXT,
  loc_paragraph_end      TEXT,
  loc_clause_end         TEXT,
  loc_subclause_end      TEXT,
  loc_note               TEXT,

  extraction_method      TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (extraction_method IN ('skim','full-read','re-read','auto-mined')),
  extraction_status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'preliminary'
                           CHECK (extraction_status IN ('preliminary','reviewed','verified','contradicted','absent-confirmed')),
  promoted_to_rdc_id     TEXT REFERENCES reasoning_doc_citations(citation_id),
  notes                  TEXT,

  created_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_session     TEXT,
  updated_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_by_session     TEXT, figure_role TEXT
  CHECK (figure_role IS NULL OR figure_role IN ('claim', 'finding', 'condition', 'derived')), comparator TEXT
  CHECK (comparator IS NULL OR comparator IN ('=', '<', '<=', '>', '>=', 'between', 'approx')), harm_finding INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
  CHECK (harm_finding IN (0, 1))
  CHECK (harm_finding = 0 OR figure_role = 'finding'),

  -- Carried across verbatim: if claim_type='absent', claimed_value must be NULL; if it
  -- is anything else, claimed_value must be present. `db.py add-extraction` refuses both
  -- violations in words BEFORE the INSERT, so an operator gets a sentence rather than
  -- "CHECK constraint failed".
  CHECK (
    (claim_type =  'absent' AND claimed_value IS NULL) OR
    (claim_type <> 'absent' AND claimed_value IS NOT NULL)
  ),

  -- D-0182, mechanised. Absence in a lens is fine; absence in ALL of them is not.
  -- Identical in form to specifications' and item_taxonomy_links' own CHECK.
  CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL)
)

===== extraction_relations table
CREATE TABLE extraction_relations (
  relation_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE FIGURE THIS EDGE QUALIFIES. NOT NULL and a real FK -- an edge naming no source
  -- row describes nothing. No UNIQUE index touches this column alone: one extraction may
  -- carry several comparator edges (a ramp slope is both condition_on a run-length limit
  -- AND audited_against a code's stated maximum), and collapsing that to one row per
  -- extraction would force a choice this table exists to avoid forcing.
  from_extraction_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),

  -- WHAT KIND OF COMPARISON THIS EDGE IS. Eight values; the CHECK is the vocabulary
  -- (CLAUDE.md section 4) and this is only its meaning, one line each.
  --   tested_at        -- the source physically measured its subjects at/against this
  --                      referent -- REF-00973's four ramp slopes were each tested_at a
  --                      named gradient.
  --   audited_against  -- the source measured whether subjects could perform WITHIN a
  --                      referent's own stated limit, rather than measuring an
  --                      independent value -- REF-00971's "existing standards".
  --   confirms         -- an independent measurement agrees with the referent's value.
  --   insufficient     -- the source asserts the referent's value is NOT ENOUGH for the
  --                      population or task in question -- REF-00784's 10-100% figure.
  --   exceeds          -- the source asserts the referent's value is more than needed.
  --   delta_over       -- the source states an increment relative to a baseline rather
  --                      than an absolute figure -- REF-00976's "more than thirty
  --                      centimetres of enlargement over the surveyed stock".
  --   condition_on     -- this figure only holds given a second figure this project also
  --                      holds as a row -- a slope given its run-length limit.
  --   derived_from     -- this figure is computed from the referent, never read off a
  --                      source -- always paired with input_role below and always a row
  --                      referent, never a label; see the CHECK immediately following.
  relation            TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (relation IN (
                        'tested_at', 'audited_against', 'confirms', 'insufficient',
                        'exceeds', 'delta_over', 'condition_on', 'derived_from')),

  -- THE REFERENT, HALF A: a row this project already holds. Nullable -- see to_label.
  -- Self-joins to the same table this column sits on, which is why the identity CHECK
  -- below refuses an edge from a row to itself.
  to_extraction_id    INTEGER REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),

  -- THE REFERENT, HALF B: prose naming what to_extraction_id would otherwise point at,
  -- for a referent this project has not captured as its own row -- a code clause never
  -- extracted on its own parameter, a source's private baseline sample, or a referent the
  -- source itself never names. Exactly one of this column and to_extraction_id is set on
  -- every row; the CHECK enforcing that sits with the rest below, not here, because it
  -- names both columns together.
  to_label            TEXT,

  -- WHAT SORT OF THING to_label NAMES, when it is set. Meaningless and left NULL when
  -- the referent is a row instead -- a row already carries this information in its own
  -- data.
  --   standard      -- a code, guideline or published standard's own stated figure.
  --   own_sample    -- the source's own baseline measurement of its own subjects or
  --                   stock, as in REF-00976's surveyed housing.
  --   prior_source  -- an earlier study or publication, distinct from a code and from the
  --                   citing source's own sample.
  --   unnamed       -- the source itself does not say what the referent is. See the
  --                   `stated` column: this value and 'unnamed' there always travel
  --                   together, by CHECK.
  to_kind             TEXT CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind IN (
                        'standard', 'own_sample', 'prior_source', 'unnamed')),

  -- HOW EXPLICITLY THE SOURCE ITSELF NAMES THE REFERENT -- independent of whether this
  -- project could resolve it to a row. NOT NULL: every edge takes a position on this.
  --   named     -- the source identifies the referent by name (a code number, an author,
  --              a described sample).
  --   unnamed   -- the source gestures at a referent ("existing standards") without
  --              naming which one. Never a row referent -- see the CHECK below; naming
  --              nothing is not the same claim as naming a specific row.
  --   inferred  -- the source names no referent at all and this project supplied one from
  --              context (a code the jurisdiction and date make unambiguous). The
  --              weakest of the three and the one most likely to need revisiting.
  stated              TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (stated IN ('named', 'unnamed', 'inferred')),

  -- WHICH SIDE OF A DERIVATION this edge supplies. Meaningful only for relation =
  -- 'derived_from', enforced by CHECK -- every other relation leaves it NULL.
  --   base    -- the starting figure the derived value is computed from.
  --   delta   -- the increment added to (or subtracted from) the base.
  --   factor  -- a multiplier applied to the base, for a derivation `v_derived_figure_check`
  --            does not itself recompute -- that view covers base+delta only; a
  --            factor-based derivation is a known residual, not a silent gap, recorded
  --            here rather than built speculatively (CLAUDE.md section 8).
  input_role          TEXT CHECK (input_role IS NULL OR input_role IN ('base', 'delta', 'factor')),

  -- THE SOURCE'S OWN WORDS FOR THE COMPARISON, NOT NULL. Mirrors the verbatim discipline
  -- `observed_terms.context_quote` and `db.py add-extraction`'s required `--claim-text`
  -- already carry on this project's other judgment-stage rows: a comparator asserted with
  -- nothing of the source's own phrasing behind it is not a comparator this project has
  -- actually read.
  quote               TEXT NOT NULL,

  notes               TEXT,

  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,

  -- An edge cannot compare a figure to itself.
  CHECK (to_extraction_id IS NULL OR to_extraction_id <> from_extraction_id),

  -- The referent is named as a row or as a label; never as both at once and never as
  -- neither, or the edge would point at two things or at nothing.
  CHECK ((to_extraction_id IS NULL) <> (to_label IS NULL)),

  -- You cannot be conditioned by, or computed from, a figure that does not exist as a
  -- row: condition_on and derived_from both require a resolvable to_extraction_id.
  CHECK (relation NOT IN ('condition_on', 'derived_from') OR to_extraction_id IS NOT NULL),

  -- input_role names which side of a derivation this edge is, so it is meaningless
  -- outside relation = 'derived_from' and mandatory inside it.
  CHECK (
    (relation = 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NOT NULL)
    OR (relation <> 'derived_from' AND input_role IS NULL)
  ),

  -- An unnamed referent cannot simultaneously be one specific known row: if the source
  -- does not say what it is, this project cannot have resolved it to a row either.
  CHECK (stated <> 'unnamed' OR to_extraction_id IS NULL),

  -- Calling the referent's kind 'unnamed' is a claim about how the source stated it, so
  -- it must agree with the stated column rather than disagree with it.
  CHECK (to_kind IS NULL OR to_kind <> 'unnamed' OR stated = 'unnamed')
)

CREATE VIEW v_derived_figure_check AS
SELECT
    d.extraction_id                                              AS derived_id,
    CAST(d.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS stored,
    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS base_value,
    CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL)                                 AS delta_value,
    CAST(b.claimed_value AS REAL) + CAST(e.claimed_value AS REAL) AS recomputed
FROM source_value_extractions d
JOIN extraction_relations rb
  ON rb.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
 AND rb.relation = 'derived_from'
 AND rb.input_role = 'base'
JOIN source_value_extractions b ON b.extraction_id = rb.to_extraction_id
JOIN extraction_relations rd
  ON rd.from_extraction_id = d.extraction_id
 AND rd.relation = 'derived_from'
 AND rd.input_role = 'delta'

WHERE d.figure_role = 'derived'
  AND d.claimed_value GLOB '*[0-9]*' AND d.claimed_value NOT GLOB '*[^0-9.eE+-]*'

CREATE VIEW v_value_independence AS

_LENS_COLUMNS = {

def amend_extraction(extraction_id: int, field: str, value: str, reason: str,
                     session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Change a field of `_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS` on an EXISTING row -- and ONLY those.

    Every other refusal here mirrors the one `insert_extraction` runs at write
    time, because grading a pre-existing row after the fact must not be able to
    reach a state add-extraction itself refuses to create.
    """
    if field not in _AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS:
        raise Refusal(
            f"amend-extraction: --field {field!r} refused. Only "
            f"{sorted(_AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS)} may be amended here -- a wrong "
            f"claimed_value or claim_text is a SECOND ROW and a contest (D-0168), "
            f"not an overwrite. Write another `db.py add-extraction` if the "
            f"disagreement is over the value or the claim itself.")
    reason = (reason or "").strip()
    if not reason:
        raise Refusal(
            "amend-extraction: --reason is required. An amendment that cannot say "
            "why cannot be contested.")
    value = (value or "").strip()
    if not value:
        raise Refusal("amend-extraction: --value is required and must not be blank.")
    with dbcore.connect(dry_run) as conn:
        # SELECT * rather than a hand-listed column set. The list here was
        # "extraction_id, ref_id, figure_role, comparator, claim_type, notes" and
        # broke with IndexError the moment _AMENDABLE_SVE_FIELDS grew -- a second
        # place naming the amendable columns, one line below the constant that
        # names them. Two lists, one truth.
        row = conn.execute(
            "SELECT * FROM source_value_extractions WHERE extraction_id=?",
            (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"amend-extraction: extraction_id {extraction_id}: no "
                          f"such row.")
        # BOTH GATES, DERIVED, ON EVERY AMENDABLE FIELD. The first version of this gated
        # one column by name -- `if field == "root_ref_id"` -- twenty lines below a
        # generic check_declared in amend_source, which is the field-by-field shape rule 8
        # forbids and which this very commit had just criticised. fk_declared reads
        # PRAGMA foreign_key_list, so it is a no-op where no FK is declared and covers
        # every amendable reference the day one becomes amendable.
        dbcore.fk_declared(conn, "source_value_extractions", field, value,
                           f"amend-extraction --field {field}")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_value_extractions", field, value,
                              "amend-extraction")

        old = row[field]
        if field == "extraction_status" and value == "verified":
            _require_full_scan_for_verified(conn, row["ref_id"], row["parameter_id"],
                                            "amend-extraction")
        if field == "figure_role":
            if row["claim_type"] == "absent" and value != "finding":
                raise Refusal(
                    f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id} has "
                    f"claim_type='absent' -- absence IS a finding, so figure_role "
                    f"must stay 'finding', not {value!r}.")
            if value == "derived":
                base_edge = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM extraction_relations WHERE from_extraction_id=? "
                    "AND relation='derived_from' AND input_role='base'",
                    (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
                if not base_edge:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"amend-extraction: figure_role='derived' requires at "
                        f"least one derived_from edge carrying input_role=base. "
                        f"extraction {extraction_id} has none -- add one with "
                        f"relate-extraction first.")
            if value == "claim":
                bad = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT relation FROM extraction_relations "
                    "WHERE from_extraction_id=? AND relation IN "
                    "('insufficient','audited_against') LIMIT 1",
                    (extraction_id,)).fetchone()
                if bad:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"amend-extraction: extraction {extraction_id} carries a "
                        f"{bad[0]!r} edge -- a row finding the baseline inadequate "
                        f"or audited against it asserts no absolute value, so "
                        f"figure_role cannot be 'claim'. Leave it 'finding'.")

        if old == value:
            # THE REASON IS STILL RECORDED. This path used to return early and DISCARD
            # --reason, although the flag's own help says it is "Appended to notes, never
            # overwriting it". A session that re-examined a row, found the value already
            # right, and wrote down what it had learned got a silent no-op -- the finding
            # vanished. Measured on this batch: a correction recording that a quote had
            # been confirmed against a rendered page image, and that the row's page
            # locator means the one-based PDF page rather than the index an earlier note
            # called it, was written and lost.
            #
            # "I checked, and it was already correct, and here is what I found" is a real
            # result and often a more useful one than a change, because it is the only
            # trace that the checking happened at all.
            stamp = dbcore.now()
            marker = f" || {stamp[:10]} {field} CONFIRMED {value} ({reason})"

**What this is.** The entry document for a Sonnet executor. `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` is the index (why, owner decision register, Definition of Done); `tasks/T-<id>-*.md` is the one self-contained file per task; this file says **in what order, in what groups, and where to stop.** Evidence base: `01-handshake-ledger.md` and the audit in `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/`.

## 1. How to execute

1. **Merge this workplan first.** Every task file sets `$BASE` to `origin/main` once the workplan is on it, and to the workplan branch before that.
2. **Take one batch at a time, in order.** A batch is the set of tasks whose hard dependencies all lie in earlier batches. Do not start batch *n* until every READY task of batch *n-1* is merged and its after-test is green on `$BASE`.
3. **Inside a batch, work lanes in parallel and tasks in a lane serially.** A lane is a set of tasks that touch the same file (or that a task file says to sequence). Merge a lane's tasks in the order listed; where `REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` gives its own merge order for some of them (Wave 0), that order wins, because it also accounts for the characterisation harness of T-014 which must exist before the changes it compares.

    od_txt = bullet(s2, "Owner decisions")
    ods = set() if od_txt.lower().startswith("none") else set(re.findall(r"OD-\d+", od_txt))
    dl_txt = bullet(s2, "Delegated resolutions")
    m = re.search(r"for n in ([^;]*);", dl_txt)
    dels = set(re.findall(r"OD-\d+", m.group(1))) if m else set()

def closed(t):
    """Decisions whose gate is CLOSED for this task, with the reason."""
    out = [(o, gate(o, True)[1]) for o in t["ods"] if not gate(o, True)[0]]
    out += [(o, gate(o)[1]) for o in t["dels"] if not gate(o)[0]]
    return sorted(out, key=lambda x: int(x[0][3:]))


def status(t):
    """READY, or every stop that applies, '; '-joined (the first word of each part is its kind)."""
    parts = []
    if closed(t):
        parts.append("OWNER: " + ", ".join(f"{o} ({r})" for o, r in closed(t)))
    if t["designs"]:
        parts.append("DESIGN: " + ", ".join(t["designs"]))
    if not t["sonnet"]:
        parts.append("NOT FOR SONNET")
    return "; ".join(parts) or "READY"


def kinds(t):

# Remediation workplan: a pipeline that runs in every direction, at any stage, across languages and jurisdictions

_Written 2026-11-12 (UTC) by the handshake-and-adversarial leg of the bidirectional-pipeline audit. Planning only: no script, schema, governance file or database row was changed in writing it. Canadian English. Every figure is given as the command that produces it; re-run the command, do not trust a number._

## 0. Verdict

**Since this was written (2026-11-12, later the same day).** Twenty of the owner decisions were delegated to an Opus-class model, and the owner's twelfth instruction asked that the remaining ones be confirmed and, where appropriate, resolved before the plan is called complete. Which decisions stand, which hold up a task and which are answered is read from the ledger, never from this sentence: run the gate loop of section 13, or regenerate `REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` (its owner decision queue splits them into blocking, standing and open). Section 13 records the delegated pass and the gate; `DECISION-CLOSURE.md` records the twelfth-instruction pass, the decision-by-decision confirmation and a phone-ready prompt for every decision still the owner's.

**The owner's objective is not met today, and it can be met.** The objective (`grep -n -F "run in all directions" references/project-standards.md`): the pipeline "can be run in all directions at any stage in such a manner where we can dynamically research, adjudicate, synthesize, specify and render across a multitude of languages and jurisdictions". Three later statements of the same day add that the code be "efficient and centralized and clean", that the pipeline be flexible, glossed by the owner as having no "hard coded behaviours", and that it have no dead ends (`grep -n -E "^## Owner statement 2026-11-12" references/project-standards.md`).

What stands in the way, in order of harm to the book:

1. **A determination is computed without regard to the group it is for.** The engine gathers evidence by parameter alone. Fixed by the chain [T-016](tasks/T-016-wp-t1a-reading.md) → [T-017](tasks/T-017-wp-t2-conditions.md) → [T-018](tasks/T-018-link-table.md) → [T-019](tasks/T-019-lens-gather.md).
2. **Guards that a wrong figure or a misquote should not pass, pass it**: the number check (a figure written in words is now entered as a numeral, by the owner's ruling of 2026-11-12), the quote and name checks outside Latin script, a source admitted with no verification standing. [T-008](tasks/T-008-claimed-number-check.md), [T-009](tasks/T-009-script-aware-guards.md), [T-007](tasks/T-007-add-source-standing.md).
3. **The mobility group the owner decomposed by device is still one code**, and most figures sit on it. [T-055](tasks/T-055-mobility-family-tooling.md), [T-102](tasks/T-102-mobility-split.md) (OD-14 and OD-31 answered 2026-11-12).
4. **Nothing exists at render**, so every stage pair ending there has no path. [T-037](tasks/T-037-render.md), [T-038](tasks/T-038-stage-pair-gate.md) (its decisions resolved under delegation; OD-04, which held it through T-101 and T-036, answered by the owner on 2026-11-12).
5. **The base is English-shaped and its scope is in no table**: jurisdictions in code, scope unrecorded, forms unattested. [T-024](tasks/T-024-jurisdiction-registry.md), [T-025](tasks/T-025-base-writers.md), [T-026](tasks/T-026-alias-attestation.md), [T-101](tasks/T-101-scope-fill.md), [T-028](tasks/T-028-concept-identity.md).
6. **A step backward leaves no typed cause**: a gap does not say what it is a gap in. [T-013](tasks/T-013-typed-gaps.md), [T-012](tasks/T-012-follow-up-reasons.md), [T-022](tasks/T-022-contract-re-entry.md).
7. **A source must be re-read for every later parameter, parameters are flat, and synthesis finds nothing.** [T-031](tasks/T-031-clause-unit-and-open-pass.md), [T-029](tasks/T-029-term-relations.md), [T-032](tasks/T-032-synthesis-relations.md), [T-033](tasks/T-033-synthesis-candidates.md) (OD-23 answered by the owner: a clause inventory backed by retained text, a flagged re-read where neither reaches; the others' decisions are resolved under delegation).
8. **Text in other languages cannot be compared or discussed together**: nowhere holds a translation. [T-049](tasks/T-049-translation-home.md), [T-112](tasks/T-112-translate-held-text.md) (the owner asked for it on 2026-11-12; the target language, English for display, is resolved under delegation as OD-02).

**Start now:** the tasks of Wave 0 need no owner decision, no design and no earlier wave (section 4). **Then stop for the owner** at the points listed in section 6; the questions are in section 8, each with a one-line answer form.

## 1. What this folder holds, and which file governs

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md` | This index: order, dependencies, stop points, the owner decision register, the Definition of Done. |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-<id>-<slug>.md` | One file per task, self-contained. Count them: `ls workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/tasks/T-[0-9]*-*.md | grep -v -- -design | wc -l`. Ids are not contiguous (the hundreds are research tasks; unused numbers mean nothing). |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/01-handshake-ledger.md` | The evidence base, requirement by requirement. **Where it differs from `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/fa-corrections-for-suite.md`, the corrections file governs.** One example: its headline that a wrong-group determination "passes every gate" is false; the blocking integrity check stops it for unverified governing sources, though for the wrong reason. |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-PLAN.md` | The batches, lanes and owner queue, generated from the task files by `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/build_batches.py`; never hand-edited. |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS.md` | The delegated resolutions of twenty register decisions, with the independent check's verdicts, the corrections applied, and the build plan (its last section). Not the owner's words. |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DELEGATED-RESOLUTIONS-REVIEW.md` | The independent Opus-class review of OD-01, OD-02, OD-12 and OD-14 (delegation condition (d)). |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/FOLD-LOG.md` | What the fold of the resolutions into this plan changed, file by file; the owner questions it raised (now register entries OD-31 to OD-35); what it could not resolve. |
| `workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/DECISION-CLOSURE.md` | The twelfth-instruction pass: every register decision confirmed as blocking, standing or answered, with the commands; the plan issues found and fixed; a phone-ready prompt for each decision still the owner's, in the order of what it releases. |
| `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/audit/` | The audit: `hs-handshake-matrix.md` (verdict per requirement), `hs-adversarial-findings.md`, `hs-improvement-programme.md` (each IMP entry, the acceptance tests, the final recommendations in §8 and the code-quality, flexibility and dead-end findings in §9), `hs-stress-audit.md` (three rounds of stress tests), `fa-corrections-for-suite.md`. A task file never requires you to open these. |
| `scratchpad/session_2026-11-12-pipeline-bidirectional-audit/stress/` | The stress scripts and their logs, kept as a characterisation harness (`RETAINED.md` says what is kept and why). |

The seven further suite documents first planned are not written; the owner dropped that plan in favour of this one.

## 2. How to execute

0. **Merge this workplan first.** The task files assume the workplan is on the branch a task starts from. Until its pull request is merged to `main`, the integration base is the workplan branch (`origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0`); every task file sets `$BASE` by one line that tests which of the two holds the workplan, and gates and measures against it. A task started from a `main` that lacks the workplan would diff the whole workplan: the pilots showed it.
1. **One task, one session, one pull request.** Pick the next task by section 4 or 5. Open its file. Read `CLAUDE.md`. Do exactly what the file says, in its order: preconditions, evidence, change, sweep, verification, commit, adversarial pass, pull request last.
2. **One pull request merges at a time** (the prior workplan's rule WR-1: `grep -n "WR-1" workplan/2026-10-23-pipeline-resolution-workplan.md`). Branches may be prepared side by side; each later one takes the merged predecessor with `git merge origin/main` and derives its migration number again. Merging is the owner's act unless the owner has said otherwise; an executor does not merge its own pull request and does not watch it (CLAUDE.md rule 9).
3. **Tooling before research, never together** (CLAUDE.md rule 10). A research task starts only when the tooling it names is on `main`.
4. **A task that is `NOT FOR SONNET`** waits for the Fable implementation agent (design) or an Opus-class session (judgment), as its first line says. The owner authorised the Fable agent to "design, author, curate, orchestrate, delete as required" for code, schema, scripts, checks and skills (`grep -n -F "design, author, curate, orchestrate" references/project-standards.md`); doctrine stays with the owner.
5. **When a task stops**, it reports what it ran, what it saw and what it expected, and changes nothing further. A stop is a result, not a failure. Do not work around it.
5a. **The first execution of an unpiloted task is its pilot.** All but three of the task files have never been executed (section 12 says which, by command). The executor of each ends the pull request body with a heading "Task-file defects" listing what in the file was wrong, missing or ambiguous, even when the change succeeded, so the files that follow can be corrected.
6. **When the ground has moved** (a task's evidence command no longer gives the output the file states), the task stops. Either the defect is already fixed, or an earlier merge changed the facts; the orchestrating session re-reads the task against `main` before anyone resumes it.

## OD-03 — A concept that has no English name

**Status:** RESOLVED. **Confidence:** medium (the direction is clear; the display derivation is a design detail for T-028). **Independent check:** not required by condition (d).

**The decision in one line.** A concept's identity is its neutral id; its names are rows in a forms table (every attested form, any language, one row per occurrence); `canonical_en` is kept as our English descriptive label, never a form; the name shown is derived by the E1 rule, not typed.

**What I verified.**
- `terms.canonical_en TEXT NOT NULL` (`select sql from sqlite_master where name='terms'`); `term_aliases` holds forms keyed by term, alias and language (`pragma table_info(term_aliases)`), with no source or jurisdiction occurrence of its own.
- E1, confirmed by the owner by name ("e1 e3 e4; Appy yes", PS:5041): "A concept first met outside English is named by the instrument's own phrase, in its own language, until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction is observed naming the same concept" (PS:5049).
- The eighth clarification: an English descriptive label "marked as ours" is allowed; "English is one column of the matrix among others and is not read first, matched first or ranked first" (PS:5209-5214).
- The sixth statement: a concept is an equivalence class of forms, each with usage type and attestation (PS:5164-5170).
- The seventh statement left "how a concept first met outside English is held (`terms.canonical_en` is required)" to the owner's schema decision (PS:5194); this delegation covers it.
- A design exists and approves nothing: `scratchpad/session_2026-11-06-base-vocabulary-review/matrix-design/base-matrix-design.md` §3 (canonical_en as "OUR label … never a form"; forms in `term_forms`; label basis derived by a view).
- Such concepts are imminent, not hypothetical: the eighth clarification answers a report of "180 non-English-origin register rows" (PS:5202) awaiting minting.

**Three-criteria test.**
- C1 favours a forms table, strongly: every name carries where it was found, which is the provenance the sixth and seventh statements require; and it favours deriving the display name (rule 8) over a stored pointer that can disagree with the forms it points at.
- C2 favours keeping an English descriptive label on every concept, so an English page can say what the concept is, while showing the instrument's own phrase as its name (E1).
- C3 favours holding a concept English does not carve on equal footing; (b) alone would still identify it by an English gloss.
- No conflict. **Rejected:** (b) alone (the concept stays named by English: C1, C3, and E1); (c) (forces the decision under time pressure when the register is minted; the rows are waiting).

**Resolution.** `OD-03: forms table; canonical_en kept as our English descriptive label, never a form; the display name derived by E1` — that is, the register's option (a) without a stored display pointer, combined with the part of (b) that keeps an English label. The label's basis (an instrument's own term, or our descriptive label) is derived, not typed. The name shown is the origin instrument's phrase until an English-jurisdiction instrument attests an English form (E1); where several forms qualify, T-028 states the derivation, and a stored, warranted choice is used only where no derivation decides.

**Reversal condition.** T-028's design finds the display name cannot be derived without a judgment on most concepts (then a stored pointer with its warrant), or the owner reverses E1 or the eighth clarification.

**Unblocks.** T-028.

**Implied task-file changes.** T-028: take the matrix design's `term_forms` route (not a second forms home beside `term_aliases`); document `canonical_en` as label; add no label-kind column (derived). Its NOT FOR SONNET status stands.

75	## 4. Keys and uniqueness
76	
77	- **Cell** = (term_id, language, jurisdiction), a GROUP BY over `term_forms` JOIN `base_sources`; never
78	  stored. **Occurrence key** = `ux_term_forms_occurrence` (term, form, language, variety, source, clause,
79	  page, line): the same form in two sources is two rows, and counts once in the cell (`COUNT(DISTINCT form)`).
80	- **Language** is `lang_jur_map`'s code (FR, NO, ZH); **variety** is its own column (nb, nn, Hans, Hant),
81	  no CHECK, so Bokmål and Simplified/Traditional need no schema change. `base_sources (language,
82	  jurisdiction)` is a composite FK to `lang_jur_map`; a form in another language than its source (an English
83	  term in a Japanese standard) is caught by `v_base_forms_unmapped`, which must be empty or the pair declared.
84	  Arabic/Bengali/Hindi/Swahili are already map rows (`SELECT DISTINCT language FROM lang_jur_map`); admitting
85	  them is a `scope_status` value, not a schema change. Case mismatch: `term_aliases.language` is lower case,
86	  the map upper (`SELECT DISTINCT language FROM term_aliases`); the new tables follow the map.
87	- **Adopting instrument** (Land, comunidad autónoma, CN-BJ): `base_sources.subdivision`; the matrix column
88	  stays the national jurisdiction. A commune or a DPO is `issuing_body` / `source_class`, not a jurisdiction.
89	- **Equivalence class** = the term itself; its forms are its members. No class table.
90	- **Sense split** = a child term with `split_of_term_id` and `discriminating_test` (CHECK: both or neither);
91	  the child's forms are its own rows, never repeated on the parent. `sense_splits.tsv` names parents by label
92	  (`cut -f2 register-v2/sense_splits.tsv | sort -u | wc -l`); each must resolve to a term at load or wait.
93	- **Conflation** = `conflation_note` on the occurrence, optionally `conflates_term_id`; recorded, not resolved.
94	- **Seed** (OR-17/E4) = `source_id` NULL and `seed_origin` in ('owner-supplied','model'); CHECKs forbid a
95	  seed a locator or quote and forbid an attested row without `page` or `clause`.

132	NOT-SEARCHED or SEARCHED-NONE-FOUND term in that column put to at least one new source of each
133	`source_class` the column has used) adds no `term_forms` row. Derivable: the round is the set of
134	`base_form_searches` rows created by one session; saturation is `NOT EXISTS (term_forms created_by_session =
135	that session in that column)`. Proper coverage = every owed column saturated and every cell HAS-FORM or
136	SEARCHED-NONE-FOUND. No hand-set percentage.

89	-- 6. COVERAGE: derived from the base itself. Columns = lang_jur_map; owed = v_research_scope.
90	CREATE VIEW v_base_matrix AS
91	WITH found AS (
92	    SELECT f.term_id, f.language, s.jurisdiction,
93	           COUNT(*) AS n_occurrences, COUNT(DISTINCT f.form) AS n_forms
94	      FROM term_forms f JOIN base_sources s ON s.source_id = f.source_id
95	     GROUP BY f.term_id, f.language, s.jurisdiction),
96	searched AS (
97	    SELECT q.term_id, s.language, s.jurisdiction, COUNT(*) AS n_sources_read
98	      FROM base_form_searches q JOIN base_sources s ON s.source_id = q.source_id
99	     GROUP BY q.term_id, s.language, s.jurisdiction)
100	SELECT t.term_id, t.kind, m.language, m.jurisdiction,
101	       COALESCE(fd.n_forms, 0) AS n_forms,
102	       COALESCE(sr.n_sources_read, 0) AS n_sources_read,
103	       CASE WHEN fd.term_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'HAS-FORM'
104	            WHEN r.language IS NULL      THEN 'OUT-OF-SCOPE'
105	            WHEN sr.term_id IS NOT NULL  THEN 'SEARCHED-NONE-FOUND'
106	            ELSE 'NOT-SEARCHED' END AS cell_state
107	  FROM terms t
108	  CROSS JOIN lang_jur_map m
109	  LEFT JOIN v_research_scope r ON r.language = m.language AND r.jurisdiction = m.jurisdiction
110	  LEFT JOIN found fd    ON fd.term_id = t.term_id AND fd.language = m.language AND fd.jurisdiction = m.jurisdiction
111	  LEFT JOIN searched sr ON sr.term_id = t.term_id AND sr.language = m.language AND sr.jurisdiction = m.jurisdiction;

"""
scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py — provenance + verification surface for
the controlled vocabulary (terms / term_aliases).

Why this exists. `term_aliases` drives multilingual retrieval via
the (now deleted) query generator, but nothing recorded *where an alias came
from*. Provenance lived in a freeform `notes` string when it was recorded at
all, so a reader could not distinguish a term lifted from a national standards
glossary from one a model produced. On 2026-07-25, 789 non-English aliases
carried no marker of any kind.

That is a trust problem, not a formatting one: retrieval built on unverified
terminology can silently miss the literature it was meant to find, and nobody
downstream can tell which rows to distrust.

What it enforces. Every alias created on or after CUTOFF_SESSION_DATE must
carry a recognised provenance marker. Earlier rows are grandfathered and
reported as UNKNOWN — the same backfill-on-touch convention the attestation
system uses, so this lands as a forward commitment rather than a demand to
retro-document 881 legacy rows before anything else can move.

The verification markers come from references/native-alias-verification.md, so
there is a defined route out of MODEL-GENERATED rather than a permanent label:

    MODEL-GENERATED  -> VERIFIED-GLOSSARY  (national standards body glossary)
                     -> VERIFIED-NATIVE    (qualified native-speaker review)
                     -> VERIFIED-CROSS     (corroborated across published sources)

keep writing to the old name forever; a schema-phase rename runs first and
    they die on replay. Migration 025 hit this from the other side and had to
    withdraw a data migration to escape it. The 055 rename hit it from this side
    across 19 data migrations spanning two months, where withdrawal is not
    available.

    A numbered schema migration may therefore declare, on its own line:

        -- AFTER_DATA: YYYYMMDDHHMMSS

    meaning: this migration, and every migration numbered after it, applies only
    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
    present; each opens another data segment.
    """
    schema_migs = discover_schema_migrations()
    data_migs = discover_data_migrations()
    marks = []
    for i, (_v, path) in enumerate(schema_migs):
        m = AFTER_DATA_PATTERN.search(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if m:
            marks.append((i, m.group(1)))

    plan, si, di = [], 0, 0
    for idx, cutoff in marks:
        plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:idx]]
        si = idx
        while di < len(data_migs) and data_migs[di][0] <= cutoff:
            plan.append(("data",) + data_migs[di])
            di += 1
    plan += [("schema", v, p) for v, p in schema_migs[si:]]
    plan += [("data",) + d for d in data_migs[di:]]
    return plan

## 5. Caller sweep

Names to sweep: `lang_jur_map`, `base_taxonomy_identity`, `writable_tables`

**What a caller is.** A hit is a *caller* when its behaviour or its truth changes with this task: code that calls or imports the name; a test that exercises the behaviour you are changing, even if it asserts nothing about it; a view, trigger or index; a registry `cmd` or `basis`; a skill, command or governance sentence that states the behaviour being changed. A hit that stays true after your change is a *mention* and needs nothing. **Fixing a caller the sweep finds is in scope** (CLAUDE.md rule 4): make the fix in this pull request and list it there.

**What the sweep leaves out, and why.** `workplan/` (plans, and the generated `workplan/pipeline-state-graph/graph.json` and `STATE-GRAPH.md`, which list every verb and are rebuilt by their builder; only `machines.yaml` there is hand-written, and it is swept); `references/project-standards.md` (the append-only ledger: a sentence there is superseded by a new entry, never edited); `scripts/migrations/` (immutable once committed); `sessions/`, `_archived/`, `audits/`, `versions/`, `dossier/`, `transcripts/`, `scratchpad/` (frozen records).

```
N='<name>'                                                 # run once per name
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'                    # code, tests, skills, agents, commands, hooks, workflows
python3 -I -c "import sqlite3,sys;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print([(r[0],r[1]) for r in c.execute('select type,name from sqlite_master where sql like ?',('%'+sys.argv[1]+'%',))])" "$N"   # views, triggers, indexes
python3 -c "import yaml,sys;print([c['id'] for c in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if sys.argv[1] in str(c)])" "$N"   # the check registry
git grep -n -F -e "$N" -- governance architecture CLAUDE.md references workplan/pipeline-state-graph/machines.yaml ':(exclude)references/project-standards.md' ':(exclude)references/search-log'   # prose and hand-written needles
```
If this task adds, renames or removes a verb, a table, a view or the text of a refusal, also run `python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --check` (it writes nothing) and report its result. An object that returns 0 rows is unproven, not clean.

**Hits when this file was written** (2026-11-12, the two `git grep` lines above with `-l`; re-run them, a new file in your output is a hit to judge):

- `lang_jur_map`: code and skills: `schemas/enums.py`, `scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py`, `scripts/audit/graph/known_debt.yaml`, `scripts/audit/graph/topology.py`, `scripts/audit/jurisdiction_db_vocabulary.py`, `scripts/db.py`, `scripts/dbcore.py`, `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`, `skills/run-pipeline_SKILL.md`. Prose: `governance/context-map.yaml`, `governance/functional-taxonomy.md`, `governance/held-tensions.md`, `governance/owner-browser.yaml`, `governance/stage-map.yaml`.
- `base_taxonomy_identity`: code and skills: `.claude/settings.json`, `schemas/enums.py`, `schemas/evidence_state.py`, `scripts/assess/assess_cell.py`, `scripts/audit/graph/extract_db.py`, `scripts/audit/graph/topology.py`, `scripts/audit/graph_audit.py`, `scripts/audit/skill_vocabulary_audit.py`, `scripts/db.py`, `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py`, `scripts/tests/test_db_integrity.py`, `scripts/tests/test_evidence_cell_state_2_3.py`, `scripts/tests/test_run_pipeline_refusals.py`, `scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py` and others (the command lists them all). Prose: `CLAUDE.md`, `governance/context-map.yaml`, `governance/evidence-architecture.md`, `governance/functional-taxonomy.md`, `governance/held-tensions.md`, `governance/owner-browser.yaml`, `governance/population-taxonomy.md`, `governance/research-contract.yaml`, `governance/stage-map.yaml`, `references/connection-reasoning/_template.md`.
- `writable_tables`: code and skills: `scripts/db.py`, `scripts/dbcore.py`, `scripts/research/emit_batch_sql.py`, `scripts/tests/test_db_amend_writers.py`, `scripts/tests/test_scan_contract.py`. Prose: `CLAUDE.md`.

Every test file in that list is run before and after the change (section 6): a test that calls what you change is a caller even when it asserts nothing about it.

## 6. Verification

**Step 1, before any edit: the before-run.** These registered checks read what this task touches: `test_run_pipeline_refusals`, `test_db_amend_writers`, `test_scan_contract`, `test_assess_cell_pilot`. Run each as the registry runs it and keep the output. The command reads each check's `cmd` from the registry, so a renamed script is still found:

```
CHECKS="test_run_pipeline_refusals test_db_amend_writers test_scan_contract test_assess_cell_pilot"
for c in $CHECKS; do cmd=$(python3 -c "import yaml,sys,shlex;print(shlex.join(next(x['cmd'] for x in yaml.safe_load(open('governance/check-registry.yaml'))['checks'] if x['id']==sys.argv[1])))" $c); $cmd > "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" 2>&1; echo "$c rc=$? | $(grep -E 'EXAMINED|RESULTS|FAILED|VERDICT' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt" | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-200)"; done
```

Each line shows the check's subject (`EXAMINED:`). A check that is red here was red before you touched anything (on 2026-11-12 `test_scan_contract` failed two cases, G01 and G02, and `retired_vocabulary` reported occurrences): record it and carry on. A check that prints no `EXAMINED:` line, or `EXAMINED: 0`, examined nothing: say so in the pull request.

**Step 2: red before, green after.** Before: the tables are outside the captured set. After: they are in it, and a pair added on a scratch copy appears in `emit_batch_sql.py` output.

**Writing the test.** Take case ids that cannot collide: prefix them with this task's number (`T025-01`, `T025-02`, …) and confirm the prefix is free first (`grep -c '"T025-' <the test file>` prints 0). Never type into a test an id, a code or a count the database can derive: choose every probe by query (for example the first term of a domain that is not yet a parameter, is not declined in `parameter_declinations` with `revoked_at IS NULL`, and whose name carries no digit). A probe for "the legitimate case still works" must be one that no *other* refusal stops, or it fails for the wrong reason. Where the live data offers no such row, build it on the test's own scratch copy or print the file's `SKIPPED-NO-FIXTURE` line, as the file's existing cases do. A new test must be able to fail: show it red on the unchanged code, or on a seeded defect that you then remove.

**Fixtures.** Anything a test or probe writes goes to a copy, is labelled `TASK-FIXTURE`, and never reaches `data/guidebook.db`.

**Step 3, after the change: the after-run.** The same loop with `after-` in place of `before-`. Then compare, check by check: `diff <(grep -E '\[✗\]|^ *FAIL|^FAILED|VERDICT: FAIL' "$SCRATCH/before-$c.txt") <(grep -E '\[✗\]|^ *FAIL|^FAILED|VERDICT: FAIL' "$SCRATCH/after-$c.txt")`. No failing case may appear that was not failing before; the `EXAMINED:` number may only change by the cases you added.

**Step 4: the gate, once.**

```
BASE=$(git cat-file -e origin/main:workplan/2026-11-12-bidirectional-pipeline/REMEDIATION-WORKPLAN.md 2>/dev/null && echo origin/main || echo origin/ccr-408aaa9b-z3e4s0)
scripts/preflight.sh --base "$BASE" --explain > "$SCRATCH/gate.txt" 2>&1; echo "rc=$?"; grep -E '^(RESULT|PREFLIGHT|SELFTEST)|FAIL|NOTHING-IN-SCOPE' "$SCRATCH/gate.txt"
```
- **Run it once, when every edit is made, before the commit.** It compares your working tree (committed or not, untracked files included) with the point where your branch left `$BASE`, so it does not need a commit first. `preflight.sh` runs the registry selftest and then `run_checks.py --changed-from`: do not run `run_checks.py` separately on the same diff, and never `--all`. Re-run it only if you change a file afterwards.
- **A passing check prints no `EXAMINED:` line in this output.** The subject of each check is read in the per-check runs above (`$SCRATCH/after-<check>.txt`), not here. In `gate.txt` read three things: the `RESULT` line; any check under `NOTHING-IN-SCOPE` (it has not passed: say so); any blocking `FAIL`.
- **A check that was already red before your change** (the before-run shows it) tells you nothing about your diff: name it in the pull request with its before and after lines, and move on.

**The canonical database must not move:** `sha256sum data/guidebook.db` gives the value recorded in section 2.

## 7. Commit

-- 115_identity_names.sql
-- SCHEMA migration -- the identity lens registry and its ICF map take the lens's own name (plan Phase 3
-- base; RULINGS R14 narrowed to M4, confirmed in R49(c); LED-127, LED-121). `populations` is the
-- identity lens (owner, 2026-08-28), and its key was the one lens key still called population_code
-- while every referencing column already said identity_code.
--
--   populations                  -> base_taxonomy_identity   (population_code -> identity_code)
--   population_icf_links         -> identity_icf_map         (population_code -> identity_code)
--
-- NOT IN THIS FILE: evidence_population_match and its target_population / study_population columns.
-- LED-127 names them served_group / study_group and keeps them out of the lens vocabulary, which R14's
-- evidence_identity_match contradicts; the name is the owner's. Renaming the table needs an
-- AFTER_DATA marker, because data migrations dated after 095 INSERT into it.
--
-- NO AFTER_DATA MARKER for the two renames above. Two facts together make that safe, and the second
-- is the operative one: (1) no committed data migration dated after the 095 cutoff names the renamed
-- objects (must print nothing; the literal is 095's cutoff, not today's):
--   grep -lwE 'populations|population_icf_links|population_code' scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | xargs -n1 basename | cut -d_ -f2 | awk '$1>"20260920060857"'
-- and (2) migrations 113 and 114 carry AFTER_DATA markers at the latest data_ timestamp, so
-- migrate_db.build_plan replays 115 after every committed data migration whatever it names. If (2)
-- ever changes, (1) is the check that must still hold.
--
-- SQLite rewrites every REFERENCES clause, the UNIQUE autoindex and the sqlite_sequence row itself;
-- idx_picf_icf keeps its name (there is no RENAME INDEX) and its column list is rewritten. No view and
-- no trigger names either table.

ALTER TABLE populations RENAME TO base_taxonomy_identity;
ALTER TABLE base_taxonomy_identity RENAME COLUMN population_code TO identity_code;
ALTER TABLE population_icf_links RENAME TO identity_icf_map;
ALTER TABLE identity_icf_map RENAME COLUMN population_code TO identity_code;

def rename_term(term_id: str, canonical_en: str, reason: str, session: str,
                from_observation: int = None, ruling_quote: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False):
    """Correct a term's canonical name, keeping the old one as a DEPRECATED alias.

    `amend-term` refused canonical_en since 2026-09-25 ("a vocabulary decision with
    callers, not a wording fix"), and no other verb could change it, so an answer-shaped
    or mis-chosen name was permanent (critique F5; plan section 1.2 item 6: the held ADA
    text says "turning space" and not "turning circle"). This is that vocabulary
    decision, with its warrant required:

      --from-observation N  the new name comes from a phrase a source USES, in the
                            source's own language (owner E1, 2026-11-06: a concept first
                            met outside English is named by that phrase), adjudicated to
                            THIS term, whose surface form
                            contains the new name (the 2026-09-09 rule, kept by the owner
                            on 2026-10-09: names come from observed phrases);
      --ruling-quote "..."  or from the owner's own words, quoted verbatim and found
                            exactly once in references/project-standards.md, containing
                            the new name.

    Nothing else moves: parameters, adjudications and extractions point at term_id, so the
    name is reached, never copied (rule 5). The old name lands in term_aliases as
    DEPRECATED, marked `curated` for alias_provenance_audit, and the change is recorded as
    an AMENDED line on scope_note -- the trailer amend-term already writes, so its body
    split keeps working. No other term may hold the new name, as a name or an alias.

    REFUSES: neither or both warrants; a value-bearing name (_VALUE_BEARING, as add-term);
    a quote not exactly once in the ledger or not containing the name; an observation
    not adjudicated to this term, or that does not contain the name; a name another term
                    f"words. Nothing was written.")
            warrant = (f"from observation {from_observation} ({obs['surface_form']!r} in "
                       f"{obs['ref_id']})")
        else:
            warrant = f"from the owner's words in the ledger: \"{ruling_quote.strip()}\""
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        lang = _alias_language(conn, "EN")
        why = (f"curated: former canonical_en of {term_id}, renamed to {new!r} by "
               f"rename-term {warrant}. {reason}")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type, notes FROM term_aliases WHERE term_id = ? "
                            "AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                            (term_id, old, lang)).fetchone()
        if held:
            sets = {"alias_type": "DEPRECATED",
                    "notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(held["notes"], "DEPRECATED", session,
                                                      why, stamp)}
            sets.update(_updated(conn, "term_aliases", session, stamp))
            conn.execute("UPDATE term_aliases SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                         + " WHERE term_id = ? AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                         list(sets.values()) + [term_id, old, lang])
        else:
            arow = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": old, "language": lang,
                    "alias_type": "DEPRECATED", "notes": why}
            arow.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
            conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(arow)}) "
                         f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(arow))})", list(arow.values()))
        scope = dbcore.append_dated_note(
            term["scope_note"], _TERM_TRAILER, session,
            f"canonical_en was '{old}' (rename-term, {warrant}). {reason}", stamp)
        sets = {"canonical_en": new, "scope_note": scope}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "terms", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE terms SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE term_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [term_id])
        return {"term_id": term_id, "was": old, "now": new, "deprecated_alias": old,
                "alias_language": lang, "changed": True, "dry_run": dry_run}

dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record a SOURCE-ATTESTED alias: a phrase an admitted source uses for this term.

    `term_aliases` had no writer at all (critique F5, missed by the critic: only the 057
    baseline and a selftest inserted into it), so a new language alias had no sanctioned
    path. Existing aliases are model-generated, curated, or predate provenance marking
    (alias_provenance_audit counts each class); aliases are a reading aid, never evidence
    (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3.9), and this is the route by which source-attested ones
    grow.

    NOTHING IS TYPED THAT THE MACHINE CAN READ (CLAUDE.md rule 8): the alias IS the
    observation's surface form, its language is the observation's (in term_aliases' own
    letter case, measured by _alias_language), and its jurisdiction is the source's. The
    operator chooses only the alias type, from the column's CHECK. The row POINTS at the
    observation (term_aliases.observation_id, migration 125): attestation is that pointer,
    not a substring of the notes. An alias the term already holds without a pointer is
    promoted in place; one that already carries a pointer is refused.

    REFUSES: an alias type outside the CHECK, or DEPRECATED (rename-term's record); an
    unknown term or observation; an observation no adjudication names this term with; an
    observation whose phrase is not inside its quote, or whose quote is not in a file saved
    for its source (unless the observation carries a recorded VERBATIM-EXEMPT); TRANSLATION
    (a source's own phrase is not a rendering of the English one); an alias the term already
    holds in that language WITH a pointer. The notes carry `source-attested`, the
    provenance marker alias_provenance_audit reads, with the observation and source.
    """
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "term_aliases", "alias_type", alias_type,
                              "add-alias --alias-type")
        if alias_type == "DEPRECATED":
            raise Refusal("add-alias: DEPRECATED marks a former canonical name, which only "
                          "rename-term records. A phrase a source uses is a live alias.")
        if alias_type == "TRANSLATION":
            raise Refusal("add-alias: TRANSLATION frames a phrase as a rendering of the "
                          "English one. A phrase a source uses is its own jurisdiction's term "
                          "(R11, no back-translation): record it as SYNONYM, NARROWER or "
                          "BROADER.")
        if not dbcore.exists(conn, "terms", "term_id", term_id):
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id!r}: no such term.")
        obs = conn.execute(
            "SELECT o.observation_id, o.ref_id, o.surface_form, o.language, o.locator, "
            "o.context_quote, o.notes, e.jurisdiction FROM observed_terms o "
            "JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = o.ref_id WHERE o.observation_id = ?",
            (observation_id,)).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: observation {observation_id}: no such observed term.")
        if not _names_term(conn, observation_id, term_id):
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: no adjudication of observation {observation_id} names "
                f"{term_id}. An alias says the source's phrase names THIS concept, which is "
                f"a judgement: db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {observation_id} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {term_id} --rationale ... first.")
        quote = obs["context_quote"] or ""
        kind, where, inside = _retrieval_log().classify_observation(
            obs["surface_form"], quote, obs["notes"], obs["ref_id"])
        if not quote.strip() or not inside:
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id} carries no context quote that "
                f"contains its phrase, so nothing attests the phrase was seen. Observe the "
                f"sighting again with --locator and --context-quote (db.py observe-term), "
                f"adjudicate it, and alias from that observation.")
        if kind not in ("scoped", "exempt"):
            raise Refusal(
                f"add-alias: observation {observation_id}'s quote is not in a file saved for "
                f"{obs['ref_id']} ({where}), so 'source-attested' would be untrue. Register "
                f"the source's text (scripts/research/full_text.py) and observe the sighting "
                f"from it, or record why no artefact can carry it (observe-term "
                f"--verbatim-exempt). Nothing was written.")
        lang = _alias_language(conn, obs["language"] or "EN")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT alias_type, observation_id FROM term_aliases "
                            "WHERE term_id = ? AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                            (term_id, obs["surface_form"], lang)).fetchone()
        if held and held[1] is not None:
            raise Refusal(f"add-alias: {term_id} already holds {obs['surface_form']!r} "
                          f"({lang}) as {held[0]}, attested by observation {held[1]}. "
                          f"Nothing was written.")
        others = [r[0] for r in conn.execute(
            "SELECT DISTINCT term_id FROM term_aliases WHERE alias = ? AND language = ? "
            "AND term_id <> ?", (obs["surface_form"], lang, term_id))]
        note = (f"source-attested: observation {observation_id}, {obs['ref_id']} at "
                f"{obs['locator']!r}; " + (f"quote verified in {where.split(',')[0]}"
                                          if kind == "scoped" else
                                          "the observation's quote is VERBATIM-EXEMPT"))
        if held:
            # A model-generated or unrecorded alias whose text a source uses is PROMOTED in
            # place: the pointer is attached, the held row's type and its history stay, and
            # the jurisdiction is the source's where the row had none. No second row.
            conn.execute("UPDATE term_aliases SET observation_id = ?, "
                         "jurisdiction = COALESCE(jurisdiction, ?), "
                         "notes = COALESCE(notes || '; ', '') || ?, "
                         "updated_at = ?, updated_by_session = ? "
                         "WHERE term_id = ? AND alias = ? AND language = ?",
                         (observation_id, obs["jurisdiction"], note, dbcore.now(), session,
                          term_id, obs["surface_form"], lang))
            return {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
                    "promoted": True, "alias_type_kept": held[0],
                    "also_an_alias_of": others, "dry_run": dry_run}
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
               "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
               "observation_id": observation_id, "notes": note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "term_aliases", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO term_aliases ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        return {"term_id": term_id, "alias": obs["surface_form"], "language": lang,
                "alias_type": alias_type, "jurisdiction": obs["jurisdiction"],
                "also_an_alias_of": others, "dry_run": dry_run}

def insert_term(from_observation: int, canonical_en: str, rationale: str, session: str,
                definition: str = None, domain: str = None, scope_note: str = None,
                dry_run: bool = False, distinct_from: list = None):
    """Mint a term for a concept new to the vocabulary, AND adjudicate it in one act.

    The missing half of D-0173. `adjudicate-term --outcome NAMES-NEW` refuses unless the
    term already exists -- "create the term first, then adjudicate NAMES-NEW to it" --
    and nothing created one, so NAMES-NEW was an outcome the CLI documented and could
    not reach. A checker whose satisfying writer does not exist is a trap (CLAUDE.md §8).

    Term and adjudication land together because they are one judgement: *this observed
    phrase names a concept we did not hold, and here is the term for it.* Splitting them
    would permit a term with no provenance, which is the contamination the owner objected
    to on 2026-09-09 -- prior-version containers that exist before the work does.
    """
    canonical_en = (canonical_en or "").strip()
    rationale = (rationale or "").strip()
    if not canonical_en:
        raise Refusal("--canonical-en is required: a term is its name.")
    if not rationale:
        raise Refusal(
            "--rationale is required. Minting a term is an adjudication, and an "
            "adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested.")
    vb = _VALUE_BEARING_NAME.search(canonical_en)
    if vb:
        raise Refusal(
            f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} REFUSED: it carries a number, a comparator "
            f"or a min/max word ({vb.group(0)!r}), so it states a determination in its own name.\n"
            f"That is the defect the item layer was deleted for -- a container that "
            f"announces its answer predisposes every finding filed into it "
            f"(DR-2026-08-19 §1.1: 42 of 93 item names embedded a determination).\n"
            f"Name the PARAMETER, not the value: 'corridor width', not "
            f"'corridor width >=1200 mm'. The value belongs in the determination.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        obs = conn.execute("SELECT observation_id, surface_form, ref_id FROM observed_terms "
                           "WHERE observation_id=?", [from_observation]).fetchone()
        if obs is None:
            raise Refusal(
                f"observation {from_observation}: no such observed term. A term is minted "
                f"FROM an observed phrase (db.py observe-term), never from nothing -- that "
                f"is what makes the vocabulary an output of the work rather than a "
                f"presupposition.")
        if canonical_en.casefold() not in obs["surface_form"].casefold():
            raise Refusal(
                f"--canonical-en {canonical_en!r} is not inside the observed phrase "
                f"{obs['surface_form']!r}. A name is a phrase an admitted source uses, in its "
                f"own language (owner OR-17: the model may not coin names; ruling 2026-11-06, "
                f"E1). Use the phrase as written, or a contiguous part of it. A concept first "
                f"met outside English is named by that phrase until an English-language "
                f"instrument is observed naming it.")
        clash = _name_holder(conn, canonical_en, aliases=False)
        if clash:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is already TERM {clash['term_id']} "
                f"({clash['detail']!r}). That makes this NAMES-EXISTING, not "
                f"NAMES-NEW:\n  db.py adjudicate-term --observation-id {from_observation} "
                f"--outcome NAMES-EXISTING --term-id {clash['term_id']} --rationale ...")
        near = [(t, h) for t, h in _near_terms(conn, canonical_en)
                if t not in set(distinct_from or [])]
        if near:
            raise Refusal(
                f"{canonical_en!r} is a near match of " +
                "; ".join(f"{t} {h!r}" for t, h in near[:5]) +
                ". Equivalence before minting: if it names one of these, adjudicate "
                "NAMES-EXISTING (a narrower or broader phrase is an alias: add-alias "
                "--alias-type NARROWER/BROADER); if it is a distinct concept, say so with "
                "--distinct-from " + " --distinct-from ".join(t for t, _ in near[:5]) +
                " and the --rationale must say why. Nothing was written.")
        term_id = _mint_term_id(conn)
        row = {"term_id": term_id, "canonical_en": canonical_en,
               "definition": definition, "domain": domain, "scope_note": scope_note}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "terms", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO terms ({','.join(row)}) "
                     f"VALUES ({','.join('?'*len(row))})", list(row.values()))
