# T-018 design — the lens link table (OR-1c)

_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first". Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count below is given as the command that produces it; re-run it, do not trust a figure. SQL marked **sketch** is the shape to build, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English._

## 0. Verdict

**Build one table, `extraction_lens_links`: one row per (figure, lens code), four typed lens columns of which each row states exactly one, a typed warrant (`basis`, `basis_text`), and retire-in-place columns; plus one view, `v_live_lens_links`, which is the only read surface.** The four lens columns on `source_value_extractions` are retired in this pull request: the migration carries every value they hold into the table as a `carried` link, NULLs the columns, and replaces their "at least one" CHECK with a CHECK that keeps them NULL. They are not dropped, because committed data migrations INSERT them. "At least one lens per figure" (D-0182) moves to the writers and to one blocking integrity case. Two verbs are added (`add-lens-link`, `retire-lens-link`); `add-extraction` and `derive-extraction` take each lens flag repeatedly. `specifications` keeps its four columns: a cell is a key, with one code per model; a figure that concerns two ICF codes reaches two cells.

**The gather rule T-019 builds on:** a figure reaches a cell when every code the cell states is among the figure's live links (identity widened to the code's descendants by T-055). A figure is never copied.

**Confidence.** High (about 85%) on the shape: it is the 2026-08-28 four-typed-column shape moved onto a link row, which is what OR-1c asks for, and it keeps every lens a real foreign key. Medium (about 70%) on the `basis` vocabulary: it is the smallest that records the three warrants the rulings name (a quote naming the users, D-2; a heading, OD-31; a study's participants, the 2026-08-25 grade rule). Medium (about 70%) that dropping the figure-row CHECK in favour of a writer refusal plus a blocking integrity case is acceptable; the alternative (keep the columns live) is a second home.

**Owner's call.** Nothing doctrinal is decided here. One reading is marked: **[ASSUMPTION] OR-1c ("link table unless that is more prone to errors", 2026-11-06) supersedes, for a figure's lens codes, the clause "Never a `population_*` link table" of the 2026-08-28 ACTION.** Rule 0 applies (a live owner statement supersedes the record it touches); the pull request records it with a `SUPERSEDES` pair (section 5, step 6). The rest of the 2026-08-28 ACTION stands and is met: four typed lens columns, real FKs, "never two lenses in one row" (now true of every link row), the lens names in the table's name (no `population`).

## 1. What the rulings require, and where this design meets each

| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| OR-1c, `grep -n -F 'link table unless that is more prone to errors' references/project-standards.md` | several codes of one model on a figure, by a link table; the figure written once | `extraction_lens_links`; the figure row is never copied |
| 2026-08-28 lens ruling, `grep -n -F 'real FKs. Never a `population_*` link table.' references/project-standards.md` | four lens columns, one CHECK, real typed FKs, nothing polymorphic; never two lenses in one row; lens names, not `population` | four typed FK columns on the link row; CHECK exactly one per link row; no `(lens, code)` text pair |
| D-0182, `grep -n -F 'The lens CHECK is "at least one"' references/project-standards.md` | a figure carries at least one lens, ideally many | writers refuse a figure with no live link and refuse to retire its last one; integrity case (section 9, T018-05) |
| OR-1, `grep -n -F 'a figure reaches a determination only through the lens tags written on that figure' references/project-standards.md` | a figure reaches a cell only through its own lens codes; every relevant model is named | the gather predicate of section 4; T-106 fills further models as links |
| OD-29 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-29: both retire in place' references/project-standards.md`, with the 2026-09-16 ruling it reads | link rows retire in place; every reader filters on the mark first | `retired_at` columns; `v_live_lens_links` is the filtered read |
| D-2 / OD-06 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-06' references/project-standards.md \| tail -3` | judgment assigns lenses, only where a quote names the users | `basis = 'named_in_text'` with the words, checked against the row's own text |
| OD-31 (owner), `grep -n -F 'OD-31: a provision that names no one' references/project-standards.md` | a provision that names no one carries its heading's group | `basis = 'heading'` with the heading's words |
| CLAUDE.md rule 5 | one home for a figure's lens | the columns are NULLed and held NULL by CHECK; the link table is the only home |

## 2. The table and the view (sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: extraction_lens_links -- the lens codes of a figure, one row per code (OR-1c)
CREATE TABLE extraction_lens_links (
    link_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    extraction_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    -- THE FOUR LENSES, typed, one per row (2026-08-28 shape; "never two lenses in one row").
    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    medical_code        TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
    -- THE WARRANT (rule 8: a judgment records its answer and its evidence in named columns).
    --   named_in_text       the figure's own words name the users / function / need (D-2)
    --   heading             the provision names no one; its heading names the group (OD-31)
    --   study_participants  a study's own participants are this group (2026-08-25 grade rule)
    --   carried             moved by migration from the retired column; no judged warrant yet
    basis               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (basis IN
                            ('named_in_text', 'heading', 'study_participants', 'carried')),
    basis_text          TEXT,          -- the exact words that warrant the link
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((identity_code IS NOT NULL) + (icf_code IS NOT NULL)
         + (needs_code IS NOT NULL) + (medical_code IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK ((basis = 'carried') = (basis_text IS NULL)),
    CHECK (basis_text IS NULL OR length(trim(basis_text)) > 0),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL)
       AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL))
);
-- One LIVE link per (figure, code). A retired link may repeat a live one (history).
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_extraction_lens_live ON extraction_lens_links
    (extraction_id, COALESCE(identity_code, ''), COALESCE(icf_code, ''),
     COALESCE(needs_code, ''), COALESCE(medical_code, ''))
    WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_extraction ON extraction_lens_links(extraction_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_identity   ON extraction_lens_links(identity_code) WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_icf        ON extraction_lens_links(icf_code)      WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_needs      ON extraction_lens_links(needs_code)    WHERE retired_at IS NULL;

-- The one read surface (OD-29: every reader filters on the retired mark first).
CREATE VIEW v_live_lens_links AS
SELECT link_id, extraction_id, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
       basis, basis_text, created_at, created_by_session
  FROM extraction_lens_links
 WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
```

Decided, not left open: the table name (`extraction_lens_links`: "lens" names all four, as the naming ruling of 2026-08-28 asks; `population_*` is retired vocabulary); `link_id` as an integer key so `retire-lens-link` and the batch capture address one row; no `superseded_by_link_id` (a retired link names its reason; the replacing link is the live one for the same figure, found by query); no column saying "this is a link" (the table is the mark). `basis_text` is a quote of the row's words, not a copy of a fact held elsewhere: it records which words the judge relied on, which no other column says.

## 3. What becomes of the four lens columns on the figure

1. **Carried.** The migration inserts one `carried` link per non-NULL lens column of every figure, stamped with that figure's own `created_at` / `created_by_session` and `updated_*` (the lens was asserted when the figure was written). Count before: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select sum(identity_code is not null)+sum(icf_code is not null)+sum(needs_code is not null)+sum(medical_code is not null) from source_value_extractions').fetchone())"`; after, `select count(*) from extraction_lens_links where basis='carried'` prints the same number.
2. **NULLed and held NULL.** The table is rebuilt (SQLite cannot drop or change a CHECK in place) with the four columns kept, their values set to NULL in the copy, and the D-0182 CHECK `COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL` replaced by `CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NULL)`, with a comment: "HISTORY, retired by migration NNN: a figure's lens lives in extraction_lens_links (OR-1c). Kept because committed data migrations INSERT these columns (rule 5); never written again." The inverted CHECK makes the retirement a typed fact rather than a convention: no writer can bring the dead home back.
3. **Why not dropped.** `git grep -l -E 'INSERT INTO "?source_value_extractions"?' -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l` prints the number of committed data migrations that INSERT these columns; replay needs the columns to exist.
4. **Why `AFTER_DATA` is required.** `scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild` applies every numbered schema migration before every data migration unless a schema migration carries `-- AFTER_DATA: <timestamp>` (`grep -n 'AFTER_DATA' scripts/migrate_db.py`). Without the marker, the rebuild would carry from an empty table and then replay the data migrations into the columns, so the rebuilt database would hold values in the columns and no links, and the CHECK of step 2 would refuse those replayed INSERTs. The migration therefore declares, on its own line, the timestamp of the newest committed data migration at execution time: `ls scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | sed -E 's/.*data_([0-9]{14})_.*/\1/' | sort | tail -1`. Migration 114 is the precedent (`grep -n AFTER_DATA scripts/migrations/114_extraction_slug_and_root.sql`).

`specifications` is not touched: its four columns are the cell key (section 4), and its D-0182 CHECK stays.

## 4. How the engine's gather uses the links (consumed by T-019, then T-055)

**The rule.** A cell is the set of codes its four key columns state (at least one). A figure reaches the cell when, for every lens the cell states, the figure has a live link carrying that code. Lenses the cell leaves NULL impose nothing. So a figure linked to `{WHEEL, d465}` reaches the cells `(WHEEL)`, `(d465)` and `(WHEEL, d465)`, and a figure linked to `{d450, d465}` reaches `(d450)` and `(d465)`: written once, counted in each.

```sql
-- sketch: the lens predicate T-019 adds to assess_cell._gather's WHERE (x = source_value_extractions)
  AND (:identity IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.identity_code = :identity))
  AND (:icf      IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.icf_code      = :icf))
  AND (:needs    IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.needs_code    = :needs))
  AND (:medical  IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.medical_code  = :medical))
```

**T-055's widening, identity only.** The identity `EXISTS` becomes `k.identity_code IN (SELECT code FROM family)` with
`WITH RECURSIVE family(code) AS (SELECT :identity UNION SELECT i.identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity i JOIN family f ON i.parent_code = f.code)`.
A child's cell gathers only that child (its family is itself plus its own descendants, none today).

**Why "cell within figure" and not exact match.** `specifications` holds one code per model. Under exact match a figure with two ICF codes could reach no cell at all, which is the defect OR-1c exists to remove. Under "any code in common" a figure tagged `(MOB, d450)` would reach the cell `(BLIND, d450)` through d450 alone, which is the wrong-group defect T-019 fixes.

**AT-32's second half** ("a determination's lens set lists every model its governing figures carry") is T-019's: the engine reads, for each determination, the distinct models of its governing figures' live links from `v_live_lens_links` and reports any model the cell key leaves NULL. Several codes of one model are several cells (section 11, alternative D).

## 5. Migration shape (one schema migration; derive its number, never type it)

Number: `ls scripts/migrations | grep -E '^[0-9]{3}_' | sort | tail -1`, plus one, zero-padded; file `scripts/migrations/NNN_extraction_lens_links.sql`; it ends `PRAGMA user_version = NNN;`. In order:

## 6. The writers (exact verbs and flags)

All in `scripts/db.py`; locate by symbol. `_LENS_COLUMNS` (the lens → registry map) is reused for every code check; nothing restates a vocabulary (`basis` choices come from `dbcore.check_values(conn, "extraction_lens_links", "basis")`, minus `carried`, which only the migration writes).

**`add-extraction` and `derive-extraction`, changed.**
- `--identity`, `--icf`, `--needs`, `--medical` become `action="append"` (each may be repeated; argparse today keeps only the last of a repeated flag, silently).
- New, required whenever any lens flag is given (which is always, since a figure needs one): `--lens-basis {named_in_text,heading,study_participants}` and `--lens-basis-text "<words>"`; they apply to every link the call writes. A code with a different warrant is added afterwards with `add-lens-link`.
- `insert_extraction` validates each code as today (registry row exists, registry not empty), refuses a `deprecated` identity code with the successor named (T-054's general refusal, reused), refuses a duplicate code within the call, writes the figure with the four columns NULL, then one link per code, in one transaction. The refusal "an extraction must be stated in at least one lens (D-0182)" is kept word for word. The result's `lens` key becomes a list of `{link_id, lens, code}`.

**`add-lens-link`, new.**
`db.py add-lens-link --extraction-id N (--identity C | --icf C | --needs C | --medical C) --basis {named_in_text,heading,study_participants} --basis-text "<words>" --session S [--dry-run]`
Refuses, each in words naming the next action: an extraction that does not exist; none or more than one code flag; a code not in its registry (`dbcore.fk_declared`); a `deprecated` identity code (successor named); a blank `--basis-text`; a `--basis-text` that is not found, case-insensitively, in the figure's `claim_text`, `source_section` or `root_population_note`, nor in a file saved for the figure's source (the helper `add-alias` already uses: `grep -n 'classify_observation' scripts/db.py`), nor, for `study_participants`, in a `study_population` of an `evidence_population_match` row of the same `ref_id`; a live link for the same figure and code, **except** when that live link's basis is `carried`, in which case the carried link is retired in the same transaction with reason `superseded by judged link <new id>` (a judged warrant replaces a carried one in one act).

**`retire-lens-link`, new.**
`db.py retire-lens-link --link-id N --reason "<why>" --session S [--dry-run]`
Sets `retired_at`, `retired_by_session`, `retirement_reason` and the `updated_*` pair. Refuses: no such link; already retired; a blank reason; **the figure's last live link** ("add the replacing link first with add-lens-link; a figure with no lens is a value about nobody", D-0182).

**Not changed.** `amend-extraction` stays a field writer; it gains no lens arguments (this corrects the task file's item 2, which said it would). `specifications`, `search_executions`, `connection_targets`, `conflicts`, `determination_gates` keep their own single lens columns: OR-1c concerns figures.

**Captured set.** `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)` derives the tables from the writers' `INSERT INTO` text and orders them by the FK graph, so `extraction_lens_links` enters it after `source_value_extractions` with no list edited; `emit_batch_sql.py` captures the retirements as `UPDATE`s by `link_id`. Confirm: `python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;c=sqlite3.connect('file:'+sys.argv[1]+'?mode=ro',uri=True);t=dbcore.writable_tables(c);print('extraction_lens_links' in t, t.index('extraction_lens_links')>t.index('source_value_extractions'))" "$SCRATCH/t.db"` prints `True True` on the migrated scratch copy.

## 11. Alternatives rejected

- **A. One row per figure per combination of codes** (write the figure once per (identity, ICF, need) combination). The owner's condition was "unless that is more prone to errors"; the ledger measured the multiplication with `python3 -c` in the OR-1c entry (re-run it there). Every repeated value and quote is a copy (rule 5), and a correction to one copy misses the others.
- **B. A polymorphic link `(extraction_id, lens TEXT, code TEXT)`.** One column less, but the code is a foreign key to no table: a typo is stored. The 2026-08-28 ruling's "every lens column is a real typed foreign key — nothing is polymorphic" forbids it.
- **C. Keep the four columns as the figure's first code per model and use links only for extra codes.** Two homes for one fact (rule 5): every reader must union two places, and a re-tag must decide which to edit. Rejected; this is the "parity check is not a fix" case.
- **D. A link table for determinations too.** A cell is a key; `validate_cell_undetermined`'s uniqueness and `derivation_sha` are over one code per model. A set-valued key would make two determinations of the same figures incomparable. Several codes of one model are several cells; the figure reaches each.
- **E. Drop the four columns.** Committed data migrations INSERT them (section 3, item 3); a drop breaks the rebuild.
- **F. Keep the D-0182 CHECK on the figure and keep writing the columns from the first link.** That is alternative C with a cosmetic difference.
- **G. A trigger enforcing "at least one live link".** SQLite has no deferred triggers; an `AFTER INSERT` on the figure fires before its links exist. The writer refusal plus the blocking integrity case is the floor a trigger cannot hold.
- **H. No `basis` columns.** Smaller, but a judged link and a carried one would look the same, and the warrant OD-06 and D-2 require would live only in the session's prose.

- **T-055:** the identity predicate widens on `v_live_lens_links`.

As written it could not work: T-054's retirement refuses a code that live rows still carry, and item 4 moved rows only off a code that was already retired.
- **T-106, T-115, T-102:** write and retire links with these verbs; a judged link replaces a carried one in one call.

## 13. Not resolved here

- Whether the owner reads OR-1c's measurement as meeting "unless that is more prone to errors" is the owner's (the ledger marks it [ASSUMPTION]); this design does not reopen it.
- The figure-row CHECK becomes a writer refusal plus a blocking integrity case: a hand-written INSERT that bypasses `db.py` and adds a figure with no link would pass the schema and fail only the integrity case. That is the same exposure every cross-table rule in this schema has.

## 0. Verdict

**Build one table, `extraction_lens_links`: one row per (figure, lens code), four typed lens columns of which each row states exactly one, a typed warrant (`basis`, `basis_text`), and retire-in-place columns; plus one view, `v_live_lens_links`, which is the only read surface.** The four lens columns on `source_value_extractions` are retired in this pull request: the migration carries every value they hold into the table as a `carried` link, NULLs the columns, and replaces their "at least one" CHECK with a CHECK that keeps them NULL. They are not dropped, because committed data migrations INSERT them. "At least one lens per figure" (D-0182) moves to the writers and to one blocking integrity case. Two verbs are added (`add-lens-link`, `retire-lens-link`); `add-extraction` and `derive-extraction` take each lens flag repeatedly. `specifications` keeps its four columns: a cell is a key, with one code per model; a figure that concerns two ICF codes reaches two cells.

**The gather rule T-019 builds on:** a figure reaches a cell when every code the cell states is among the figure's live links (identity widened to the code's descendants by T-055). A figure is never copied.

**Confidence.** High (about 85%) on the shape: it is the 2026-08-28 four-typed-column shape moved onto a link row, which is what OR-1c asks for, and it keeps every lens a real foreign key. Medium (about 70%) on the `basis` vocabulary: it is the smallest that records the three warrants the rulings name (a quote naming the users, D-2; a heading, OD-31; a study's participants, the 2026-08-25 grade rule). Medium (about 70%) that dropping the figure-row CHECK in favour of a writer refusal plus a blocking integrity case is acceptable; the alternative (keep the columns live) is a second home.

**Owner's call.** Nothing doctrinal is decided here. One reading is marked: **[ASSUMPTION] OR-1c ("link table unless that is more prone to errors", 2026-11-06) supersedes, for a figure's lens codes, the clause "Never a `population_*` link table" of the 2026-08-28 ACTION.** Rule 0 applies (a live owner statement supersedes the record it touches); the pull request records it with a `SUPERSEDES` pair (section 5, step 6). The rest of the 2026-08-28 ACTION stands and is met: four typed lens columns, real FKs, "never two lenses in one row" (now true of every link row), the lens names in the table's name (no `population`).

## 2. The table and the view (sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: extraction_lens_links -- the lens codes of a figure, one row per code (OR-1c)
CREATE TABLE extraction_lens_links (
    link_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    extraction_id       INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES source_value_extractions(extraction_id),
    -- THE FOUR LENSES, typed, one per row (2026-08-28 shape; "never two lenses in one row").
    identity_code       TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_identity(identity_code),
    icf_code            TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code),
    needs_code          TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
    medical_code        TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),
    -- THE WARRANT (rule 8: a judgment records its answer and its evidence in named columns).
    --   named_in_text       the figure's own words name the users / function / need (D-2)
    --   heading             the provision names no one; its heading names the group (OD-31)
    --   study_participants  a study's own participants are this group (2026-08-25 grade rule)
    --   carried             moved by migration from the retired column; no judged warrant yet
    basis               TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (basis IN
                            ('named_in_text', 'heading', 'study_participants', 'carried')),
    basis_text          TEXT,          -- the exact words that warrant the link
    retired_at          TEXT,
    retired_by_session  TEXT,
    retirement_reason   TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    CHECK ((identity_code IS NOT NULL) + (icf_code IS NOT NULL)
         + (needs_code IS NOT NULL) + (medical_code IS NOT NULL) = 1),
    CHECK ((basis = 'carried') = (basis_text IS NULL)),
    CHECK (basis_text IS NULL OR length(trim(basis_text)) > 0),
    CHECK ((retired_at IS NULL) = (retired_by_session IS NULL)
       AND (retired_at IS NULL) = (retirement_reason IS NULL))
);
-- One LIVE link per (figure, code). A retired link may repeat a live one (history).
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_extraction_lens_live ON extraction_lens_links
    (extraction_id, COALESCE(identity_code, ''), COALESCE(icf_code, ''),
     COALESCE(needs_code, ''), COALESCE(medical_code, ''))
    WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_extraction ON extraction_lens_links(extraction_id);
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_identity   ON extraction_lens_links(identity_code) WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_icf        ON extraction_lens_links(icf_code)      WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
CREATE INDEX ix_ell_needs      ON extraction_lens_links(needs_code)    WHERE retired_at IS NULL;

-- The one read surface (OD-29: every reader filters on the retired mark first).
CREATE VIEW v_live_lens_links AS
SELECT link_id, extraction_id, identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code,
       basis, basis_text, created_at, created_by_session
  FROM extraction_lens_links
 WHERE retired_at IS NULL;
```

Decided, not left open: the table name (`extraction_lens_links`: "lens" names all four, as the naming ruling of 2026-08-28 asks; `population_*` is retired vocabulary); `link_id` as an integer key so `retire-lens-link` and the batch capture address one row; no `superseded_by_link_id` (a retired link names its reason; the replacing link is the live one for the same figure, found by query); no column saying "this is a link" (the table is the mark). `basis_text` is a quote of the row's words, not a copy of a fact held elsewhere: it records which words the judge relied on, which no other column says.

## 3. What becomes of the four lens columns on the figure

1. **Carried.** The migration inserts one `carried` link per non-NULL lens column of every figure, stamped with that figure's own `created_at` / `created_by_session` and `updated_*` (the lens was asserted when the figure was written). Count before: `python3 -I -c "import sqlite3;c=sqlite3.connect('file:data/guidebook.db?mode=ro',uri=True);print(c.execute('select sum(identity_code is not null)+sum(icf_code is not null)+sum(needs_code is not null)+sum(medical_code is not null) from source_value_extractions').fetchone())"`; after, `select count(*) from extraction_lens_links where basis='carried'` prints the same number.
2. **NULLed and held NULL.** The table is rebuilt (SQLite cannot drop or change a CHECK in place) with the four columns kept, their values set to NULL in the copy, and the D-0182 CHECK `COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL` replaced by `CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NULL)`, with a comment: "HISTORY, retired by migration NNN: a figure's lens lives in extraction_lens_links (OR-1c). Kept because committed data migrations INSERT these columns (rule 5); never written again." The inverted CHECK makes the retirement a typed fact rather than a convention: no writer can bring the dead home back.
3. **Why not dropped.** `git grep -l -E 'INSERT INTO "?source_value_extractions"?' -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l` prints the number of committed data migrations that INSERT these columns; replay needs the columns to exist.
4. **Why `AFTER_DATA` is required.** `scripts/migrate_db.py --rebuild` applies every numbered schema migration before every data migration unless a schema migration carries `-- AFTER_DATA: <timestamp>` (`grep -n 'AFTER_DATA' scripts/migrate_db.py`). Without the marker, the rebuild would carry from an empty table and then replay the data migrations into the columns, so the rebuilt database would hold values in the columns and no links, and the CHECK of step 2 would refuse those replayed INSERTs. The migration therefore declares, on its own line, the timestamp of the newest committed data migration at execution time: `ls scripts/migrations/data_*.sql | sed -E 's/.*data_([0-9]{14})_.*/\1/' | sort | tail -1`. Migration 114 is the precedent (`grep -n AFTER_DATA scripts/migrations/114_extraction_slug_and_root.sql`).

`specifications` is not touched: its four columns are the cell key (section 4), and its D-0182 CHECK stays.

## 4. How the engine's gather uses the links (consumed by T-019, then T-055)

**The rule.** A cell is the set of codes its four key columns state (at least one). A figure reaches the cell when, for every lens the cell states, the figure has a live link carrying that code. Lenses the cell leaves NULL impose nothing. So a figure linked to `{WHEEL, d465}` reaches the cells `(WHEEL)`, `(d465)` and `(WHEEL, d465)`, and a figure linked to `{d450, d465}` reaches `(d450)` and `(d465)`: written once, counted in each.

```sql
-- sketch: the lens predicate T-019 adds to assess_cell._gather's WHERE (x = source_value_extractions)
  AND (:identity IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.identity_code = :identity))
  AND (:icf      IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.icf_code      = :icf))
  AND (:needs    IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.needs_code    = :needs))
  AND (:medical  IS NULL OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_live_lens_links k
                                    WHERE k.extraction_id = x.extraction_id AND k.medical_code  = :medical))
```

**T-055's widening, identity only.** The identity `EXISTS` becomes `k.identity_code IN (SELECT code FROM family)` with
`WITH RECURSIVE family(code) AS (SELECT :identity UNION SELECT i.identity_code FROM base_taxonomy_identity i JOIN family f ON i.parent_code = f.code)`.
A child's cell gathers only that child (its family is itself plus its own descendants, none today).

**Why "cell within figure" and not exact match.** `specifications` holds one code per model. Under exact match a figure with two ICF codes could reach no cell at all, which is the defect OR-1c exists to remove. Under "any code in common" a figure tagged `(MOB, d450)` would reach the cell `(BLIND, d450)` through d450 alone, which is the wrong-group defect T-019 fixes.

**AT-32's second half** ("a determination's lens set lists every model its governing figures carry") is T-019's: the engine reads, for each determination, the distinct models of its governing figures' live links from `v_live_lens_links` and reports any model the cell key leaves NULL. Several codes of one model are several cells (section 11, alternative D).

## 6. The writers (exact verbs and flags)

All in `scripts/db.py`; locate by symbol. `_LENS_COLUMNS` (the lens → registry map) is reused for every code check; nothing restates a vocabulary (`basis` choices come from `dbcore.check_values(conn, "extraction_lens_links", "basis")`, minus `carried`, which only the migration writes).

**`add-extraction` and `derive-extraction`, changed.**
- `--identity`, `--icf`, `--needs`, `--medical` become `action="append"` (each may be repeated; argparse today keeps only the last of a repeated flag, silently).
- New, required whenever any lens flag is given (which is always, since a figure needs one): `--lens-basis {named_in_text,heading,study_participants}` and `--lens-basis-text "<words>"`; they apply to every link the call writes. A code with a different warrant is added afterwards with `add-lens-link`.
- `insert_extraction` validates each code as today (registry row exists, registry not empty), refuses a `deprecated` identity code with the successor named (T-054's general refusal, reused), refuses a duplicate code within the call, writes the figure with the four columns NULL, then one link per code, in one transaction. The refusal "an extraction must be stated in at least one lens (D-0182)" is kept word for word. The result's `lens` key becomes a list of `{link_id, lens, code}`.

**`add-lens-link`, new.**
`db.py add-lens-link --extraction-id N (--identity C | --icf C | --needs C | --medical C) --basis {named_in_text,heading,study_participants} --basis-text "<words>" --session S [--dry-run]`
Refuses, each in words naming the next action: an extraction that does not exist; none or more than one code flag; a code not in its registry (`dbcore.fk_declared`); a `deprecated` identity code (successor named); a blank `--basis-text`; a `--basis-text` that is not found, case-insensitively, in the figure's `claim_text`, `source_section` or `root_population_note`, nor in a file saved for the figure's source (the helper `add-alias` already uses: `grep -n 'classify_observation' scripts/db.py`), nor, for `study_participants`, in a `study_population` of an `evidence_population_match` row of the same `ref_id`; a live link for the same figure and code, **except** when that live link's basis is `carried`, in which case the carried link is retired in the same transaction with reason `superseded by judged link <new id>` (a judged warrant replaces a carried one in one act).

**`retire-lens-link`, new.**
`db.py retire-lens-link --link-id N --reason "<why>" --session S [--dry-run]`
Sets `retired_at`, `retired_by_session`, `retirement_reason` and the `updated_*` pair. Refuses: no such link; already retired; a blank reason; **the figure's last live link** ("add the replacing link first with add-lens-link; a figure with no lens is a value about nobody", D-0182).

**Not changed.** `amend-extraction` stays a field writer; it gains no lens arguments (this corrects the task file's item 2, which said it would). `specifications`, `search_executions`, `connection_targets`, `conflicts`, `determination_gates` keep their own single lens columns: OR-1c concerns figures.

**Captured set.** `dbcore.writable_tables(conn)` derives the tables from the writers' `INSERT INTO` text and orders them by the FK graph, so `extraction_lens_links` enters it after `source_value_extractions` with no list edited; `emit_batch_sql.py` captures the retirements as `UPDATE`s by `link_id`. Confirm: `python3 -I -c "import sys,sqlite3;sys.path.insert(0,'scripts');import dbcore;c=sqlite3.connect('file:'+sys.argv[1]+'?mode=ro',uri=True);t=dbcore.writable_tables(c);print('extraction_lens_links' in t, t.index('extraction_lens_links')>t.index('source_value_extractions'))" "$SCRATCH/t.db"` prints `True True` on the migrated scratch copy.

The owner's condition was "unless that is more prone to errors"; the ledger measured the multiplication with `python3 -c` in the OR-1c entry (re-run it there). Every repeated value and quote is a copy (rule 5), and a correction to one copy misses the others.
- **B. A polymorphic link `(extraction_id, lens TEXT, code TEXT)`.** One column less, but the code is a foreign key to no table: a typo is stored. The 2026-08-28 ruling's "every lens column is a real typed foreign key — nothing is polymorphic" forbids it.
- **C. Keep the four columns as the figure's first code per model and use links only for extra codes.** Two homes for one fact (rule 5): every reader must union two places, and a re-tag must decide which to edit. Rejected; this is the "parity check is not a fix" case.
- **D. A link table for determinations too.** A cell is a key; `validate_cell_undetermined`'s uniqueness and `derivation_sha` are over one code per model. A set-valued key would make two determinations of the same figures incomparable. Several codes of one model are several cells; the figure reaches each.
- **E. Drop the four columns.** Committed data migrations INSERT them (section 3, item 3); a drop breaks the rebuild.
- **F. Keep the D-0182 CHECK on the figure and keep writing the columns from the first link.** That is alternative C with a cosmetic difference.
- **G. A trigger enforcing "at least one live link".** SQLite has no deferred triggers; an `AFTER INSERT` on the figure fires before its links exist. The writer refusal plus the blocking integrity case is the floor a trigger cannot hold.
- **H. No `basis` columns.** Smaller, but a judged link and a carried one would look the same, and the warrant OD-06 and D-2 require would live only in the session's prose.

## 12. What this changes in other task files (applied in the same pass as this design)

- **T-018 itself:** Sonnet may now execute it against this design; item 2 names the two new verbs and drops `amend-extraction` (section 6).
- **T-019:** the gather predicate is section 4 of this file; AT-32's second half is its own.
- **T-055:** the identity predicate widens on `v_live_lens_links`.
- **T-056:** item 4 (a writer that rewrites `identity_code` on a figure, only when the code is already `deprecated`) is replaced by `add-lens-link` / `retire-lens-link`. As written it could not work: T-054's retirement refuses a code that live rows still carry, and item 4 moved rows only off a code that was already retired.
- **T-106, T-115, T-102:** write and retire links with these verbs; a judged link replaces a carried one in one call.

## 13. Not resolved here

- Whether the owner reads OR-1c's measurement as meeting "unless that is more prone to errors" is the owner's (the ledger marks it [ASSUMPTION]); this design does not reopen it.
- The figure-row CHECK becomes a writer refusal plus a blocking integrity case: a hand-written INSERT that bypasses `db.py` and adds a figure with no link would pass the schema and fail only the integrity case. That is the same exposure every cross-table rule in this schema has.

# T-028 design — a concept is its id; its names are forms; `canonical_en` is our label

_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first", on the delegated resolution of OD-03. Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English._

## 0. Verdict

**The one table that holds a form is `term_aliases`.** No new forms table is built. T-026 puts the attestation and locator columns on it (names fixed in section 4 so the two tasks agree). T-028 then rebuilds it to one row per **occurrence**, keyed by a new `form_id` (equal to each existing row's `rowid`), with a unique occurrence index in place of today's primary key `(term_id, alias, language)`, and adds `usage_type`. A concept's identity stays `terms.term_id`; its equivalence class is its member rows in `term_aliases`. **`terms.canonical_en` stays `TEXT NOT NULL`, as our English descriptive label: never written as a form, never matched against forms, never read first.** Whether the label is also an instrument's term, and the name shown (E1), are derived by one view, `v_term_names`; the only stored choice is the label itself, changed by `rename-term` with its warrant. Five writers change: the two name screens (`_name_holder`, `_near_terms`) become per-language and attestation-aware; `add-term` gains a base route that mints a concept with its first attested form and stops forcing a non-English concept's label to sit inside the source's phrase (the defect AT-25 exposes); `rename-term` stops writing our former label as a form and gains `--from-form`; `add-alias` refuses the legacy relation values and records an occurrence, not a key.

**Confidence.** Medium-high (about 75%) that `term_aliases` is the right single home: the alternative (`term_forms`, the 2026-11-06 matrix design) leaves 2382 baseline rows in a second table that can never be emptied (section 2). Medium (about 60%) on the display rule's tie-break (section 7, rule 2), which is deterministic but arbitrary when several English instruments use different forms.

**Owner's call.** None is outstanding: OD-03 is resolved under delegation (`grep -F "OD-03 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`; its check is `not required`), reversible by the owner. The points at which the owner may disagree are listed in section 15; the one most likely to matter is the tie-break of section 7.

## 1. What the rulings require

| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| OD-03 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-03: forms table' references/project-standards.md` | identity is the neutral id; names are rows of one forms table, one row per occurrence with language, jurisdiction, source; `canonical_en` our label, never a form; label basis derived; display by E1; a stored choice only where no derivation decides | sections 3, 6, 7 |
| Sixth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'a concept is an equivalence class of forms' references/project-standards.md` | equivalence class; usage type and attestation per form; disfavoured forms kept; conflation recorded per occurrence, not resolved | member rows; `usage_type`; T-026's `attestation`; conflation derived (section 5) |
| Seventh statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'base grounds itself' references/project-standards.md` | a base form carries its own source columns (URL, page, line), not an `evidence_sources` row | T-026's locator columns; `add-term` base route (section 8) |
| Eighth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'English labels are allowed on non-English-origin concepts' references/project-standards.md` | an English label allowed, marked as ours; the instrument's phrase kept as a form; no English form until an English-jurisdiction source uses one; no column read, matched or ranked first | `canonical_en` as label; `v_term_names.label_is_instrument_term`; screens per language (section 8) |
| E1 and E4, `grep -n -E '^\| E1 |^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md` | E1: named by the instrument's own phrase until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction names it. E4: model-generated and unrecorded aliases stay as flagged search aids, never vocabulary, never deleted | `v_term_names` rules (section 7); screens read attested forms only (section 8) |
| CLAUDE.md rule 5 and the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement | one home per fact; one value per cell | one forms table; `usage_type` and `attestation` in their own cells; legacy `alias_type` values frozen (section 5) |

## 2. Why `term_aliases`, not a new `term_forms`

- **One home.** `term_aliases` already holds every name the base has (`select count(*) from term_aliases`). Its rows were inserted by the 057 baseline (`grep -c 'INSERT INTO "term_aliases"' scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql`), and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires data rows in place, never deleting them. A new `term_forms` beside it leaves those rows where they are forever: either copied (two homes) or reached through a union view (the matrix design's `v_base_lookup`), which is two homes joined at read time.
- **The matrix design's two objections are answered in place.** (i) "The PK has no jurisdiction or source": the rebuild replaces the PK by a surrogate key and an occurrence index that includes jurisdiction and locator (section 3). (ii) "It mixes model seeds with attested forms": T-026's typed `attestation` separates them in a cell, and every vocabulary read filters on it (section 8).
- **The name stays.** Renaming the table would make every caller a sweep item (`git grep -l -F term_aliases -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'` and the prose `git grep` of the task file) for a legibility gain only; a row of `term_aliases` is documented as "a form of the concept, or a related search string" (section 5).

## 3. The table after T-026 and T-028 (sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: term_aliases after T-028's rebuild. Columns marked (T-026) are added by T-026 first.
CREATE TABLE term_aliases (
    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,   -- = the old rowid (pointers made by rowid still resolve)
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- the form, verbatim
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (alias_type IN
                            ('SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER','BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN')),  -- unchanged; section 5
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (attestation IN
                            ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),  -- (T-026)
    source_url          TEXT CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR source_url GLOB 'http*://*'),             -- (T-026)
    source_page         TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
    source_line         INTEGER CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR source_line > 0),                    -- (T-026)
    source_clause       TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
    usage_type          TEXT CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN
                            ('code_term','colloquial','regional_variant','outdated_or_disfavoured','product_name')),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- (T-026) an attested occurrence says where; a seed says nowhere.
    CHECK (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
           OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
           OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL))),
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
           OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL AND source_clause IS NULL))
);
-- One row per OCCURRENCE: the same form in two sources or jurisdictions is two rows.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_aliases_occurrence ON term_aliases
    (term_id, alias, language, COALESCE(jurisdiction, ''), COALESCE(observation_id, 0),
     COALESCE(source_url, ''), COALESCE(source_clause, ''), COALESCE(source_page, ''),
     COALESCE(source_line, 0));
CREATE INDEX idx_ta_alias    ON term_aliases(alias);      -- recreated (exists today)
CREATE INDEX idx_ta_language ON term_aliases(language);   -- recreated (exists today)
```

`usage_type` is nullable: NULL means "not yet typed", which is the truth for every existing row; it is typed by judgment when a row is next touched (T-107), never guessed by the migration. The five values are the sixth statement's list, in the column's own CHECK (read by `dbcore.check_values`, never retyped).

## 4. What T-026 builds on this table (names fixed here; T-026 executes them)

- `attestation TEXT NOT NULL` with the five-value CHECK above (the sixth statement's four kinds plus `unrecorded`): `instrument` (a code, standard or statute uses the form), `other_source` (any other source uses it: signage manual, public-body or advocacy guidance, a study, a glossary), `owner_supplied` (a seed the owner gave), `model_seed` (a model generated it), `unrecorded` (no provenance). `instrument` and `other_source` are attestations; the other three are seeds or unknowns and are **search aids only** (E4).
- `source_url`, `source_page`, `source_line`, `source_clause`, and the two CHECKs of section 3.
- **Mechanical fill**, from what the row already says, with no judgment: `observation_id` set → `other_source` (an admitted source used the phrase; whether it is an instrument is a judgment left to T-107); notes carrying a `VERIFIED-GLOSSARY` or `VERIFIED-CROSS` marker → `other_source`; `model-generated` → `model_seed`; anything else, including `curated`, `repo shorthand`, `VERIFIED-NATIVE` and NULL notes → `unrecorded`. The markers are the ones `classify()` in `scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py` reads; reuse that function's precedence. (The other_source rows carry no URL, so the first CHECK admits them through `observation_id` or, for the glossary markers, not at all: if `select count(*) from term_aliases where notes like '%VERIFIED-GLOSSARY%' or notes like '%VERIFIED-CROSS%'` is not 0 at execution, those rows go to `unrecorded` and are listed in T-026's pull request for T-107 to re-attest with a locator.)
- `add-alias` gains the base route of the seventh statement: `--source-url --source-page --source-line --source-clause --attestation instrument|other_source` as an alternative to `--observation-id`, and `--seed owner_supplied|model_seed` for a flagged seed with no locator.
- The search-forms junction (T-026 item 1) points at `term_aliases.form_id` once T-028 has run; until then at `rowid`, which T-028 preserves as `form_id`.

**Why the occurrence grain is T-028's and not T-026's:** T-026 adds columns by `ALTER TABLE` and needs no rebuild; the grain needs one. Until T-028 merges, a second occurrence of a form a term already holds in that language cannot be stored, so **T-107 (attest forms) now waits for T-028** (its task file is corrected in the same pass).

## 5. Membership, the legacy `alias_type` values, and conflation

- **Members of the equivalence class** are the rows whose `alias_type` is not `NARROWER` or `BROADER`. A `NARROWER` or `BROADER` row is a related search string, not a name of the concept: it is never shown as a name, never counted as a form, never matched as a name. (Term-to-term relations are T-029's table; these strings name no term.)
- **`TRANSLATION`, `DEPRECATED`, `DOMAIN` are legacy values.** Each joins a relation with another fact (a seed's origin; a usage; a domain variant). After T-026 and T-028 those facts have typed homes (`attestation`, `usage_type`). The existing rows are **not rewritten** (`DOMAIN` cannot be mapped to a usage without judgment: `select alias, language, notes from term_aliases where alias_type='DOMAIN'`); no writer writes these three values again; no reader infers attestation or usage from them. `add-alias` already refuses `TRANSLATION` and `DEPRECATED`; it now refuses `DOMAIN` too, naming `--usage-type`. `rename-term` stops writing `DEPRECATED` (section 8).
- **Conflation is derived, not stored:** a form held as a member by two concepts in one language is a conflation. Query: `select upper(language), alias, group_concat(distinct term_id) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1, 2 having count(distinct term_id) > 1`. Writers report it and do not refuse it when the operator names the other concept with `--distinct-from` (section 8).

## 6. `canonical_en`

- **Kept, `NOT NULL`, meaning "our English descriptive label".** Six committed data migrations INSERT `terms.canonical_en` (`git grep -l canonical_en -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l`) and six views read it as a parameter's name (`select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%canonical_en%'`); every one keeps working because the column keeps its meaning: a label to show and to search our own registry by. Relaxing `NOT NULL` would rebuild `terms` for no gain once English labels are allowed (eighth statement).
- **Never a form.** No writer copies `canonical_en` into `term_aliases`. `rename-term` stops doing so (it wrote the old label as `DEPRECATED`); the former label stays recorded once, in the `scope_note` trailer `rename-term` already writes.
- **Marked as ours by derivation, not a column** (OD-03: "add no label-kind column"): `v_term_names.label_is_instrument_term` is 1 exactly when an attested member form of the same concept has the label's text. Otherwise the label is ours.
- **The 94 terms** (`select count(*) from terms`) are unchanged; every one derives `label_is_instrument_term = 0` today, because no row is attested yet (`select count(*) from term_aliases where observation_id is not null` prints 0, and T-026's fill adds no locator).
- The rule that a label must sit inside an observed phrase (the owner's 2026-09-09 rule, kept 2026-10-09) **still binds when the first form is English**; it is lifted only for a concept whose first form is not English, where the eighth statement allows an English descriptive label.

## 7. The name shown: `v_term_names` (E1 derived; sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: one view, the only reader of "what is this concept called"
CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
WITH attested AS (                  -- member forms a source uses; seeds are never vocabulary (E4)
    SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
      FROM term_aliases
     WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
       AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')),
en_instrument AS (                  -- English forms an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses
    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
pick AS (
    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
      FROM terms t)
SELECT p.term_id,
       p.canonical_en AS label,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_instrument_term,
       CASE WHEN p.en_label_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_label'
            WHEN p.en_first_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_form'
            WHEN p.origin_form   IS NOT NULL THEN 'origin_instrument_form'
            ELSE 'label_ours' END AS display_basis,
       COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form) AS display_form_id,
       COALESCE((SELECT alias FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                p.canonical_en) AS display_name,
       COALESCE((SELECT upper(language) FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                'EN') AS display_language,
       p.origin_form AS origin_form_id
  FROM pick p;
```

**The rules, in order (E1, with the stored choice):**
1. Our label equals an English form an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses → show it (`english_instrument_label`). This is also how the stored, warranted choice works: `rename-term --from-form <form_id>` sets the label to one attested form (section 8).
2. Else an English instrument form of such a jurisdiction exists → show the first recorded of them (`english_instrument_form`). **Arbitrary when there are several** (for example two English-language codes naming one concept differently); the remedy is rule 1 via `rename-term`, and `select term_id from v_term_names v where display_basis='english_instrument_form' and (select count(distinct lower(alias)) from term_aliases a where a.term_id=v.term_id and upper(a.language)='EN' and a.attestation='instrument') > 1` lists the concepts owed that choice.

# T-028 design — a concept is its id; its names are forms; `canonical_en` is our label

_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first", on the delegated resolution of OD-03. Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling. Every count is given as the command that produces it; re-run it. SQL marked **sketch** is a shape, not a file to paste unread. Canadian English._

## 0. Verdict

**The one table that holds a form is `term_aliases`.** No new forms table is built. T-026 puts the attestation and locator columns on it (names fixed in section 4 so the two tasks agree). T-028 then rebuilds it to one row per **occurrence**, keyed by a new `form_id` (equal to each existing row's `rowid`), with a unique occurrence index in place of today's primary key `(term_id, alias, language)`, and adds `usage_type`. A concept's identity stays `terms.term_id`; its equivalence class is its member rows in `term_aliases`. **`terms.canonical_en` stays `TEXT NOT NULL`, as our English descriptive label: never written as a form, never matched against forms, never read first.** Whether the label is also an instrument's term, and the name shown (E1), are derived by one view, `v_term_names`; the only stored choice is the label itself, changed by `rename-term` with its warrant. Five writers change: the two name screens (`_name_holder`, `_near_terms`) become per-language and attestation-aware; `add-term` gains a base route that mints a concept with its first attested form and stops forcing a non-English concept's label to sit inside the source's phrase (the defect AT-25 exposes); `rename-term` stops writing our former label as a form and gains `--from-form`; `add-alias` refuses the legacy relation values and records an occurrence, not a key.

**Confidence.** Medium-high (about 75%) that `term_aliases` is the right single home: the alternative (`term_forms`, the 2026-11-06 matrix design) leaves 2382 baseline rows in a second table that can never be emptied (section 2). Medium (about 60%) on the display rule's tie-break (section 7, rule 2), which is deterministic but arbitrary when several English instruments use different forms.

**Owner's call.** None is outstanding: OD-03 is resolved under delegation (`grep -F "OD-03 STATUS:" references/project-standards.md | tail -1`; its check is `not required`), reversible by the owner. The points at which the owner may disagree are listed in section 15; the one most likely to matter is the tie-break of section 7.

## 1. What the rulings require

| Ruling (find it with) | Requirement | Met by |
|---|---|---|
| OD-03 (delegated), `grep -n -F 'OD-03: forms table' references/project-standards.md` | identity is the neutral id; names are rows of one forms table, one row per occurrence with language, jurisdiction, source; `canonical_en` our label, never a form; label basis derived; display by E1; a stored choice only where no derivation decides | sections 3, 6, 7 |
| Sixth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'a concept is an equivalence class of forms' references/project-standards.md` | equivalence class; usage type and attestation per form; disfavoured forms kept; conflation recorded per occurrence, not resolved | member rows; `usage_type`; T-026's `attestation`; conflation derived (section 5) |
| Seventh statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'base grounds itself' references/project-standards.md` | a base form carries its own source columns (URL, page, line), not an `evidence_sources` row | T-026's locator columns; `add-term` base route (section 8) |
| Eighth statement 2026-11-06, `grep -n -F 'English labels are allowed on non-English-origin concepts' references/project-standards.md` | an English label allowed, marked as ours; the instrument's phrase kept as a form; no English form until an English-jurisdiction source uses one; no column read, matched or ranked first | `canonical_en` as label; `v_term_names.label_is_instrument_term`; screens per language (section 8) |
| E1 and E4, `grep -n -E '^\| E1 |^\| E4 ' references/project-standards.md` | E1: named by the instrument's own phrase until an English-language instrument of a P1+P2+P3 jurisdiction names it. E4: model-generated and unrecorded aliases stay as flagged search aids, never vocabulary, never deleted | `v_term_names` rules (section 7); screens read attested forms only (section 8) |
| CLAUDE.md rule 5 and the 2026-11-06 schema-shape statement | one home per fact; one value per cell | one forms table; `usage_type` and `attestation` in their own cells; legacy `alias_type` values frozen (section 5) |

## 2. Why `term_aliases`, not a new `term_forms`

- **One home.** `term_aliases` already holds every name the base has (`select count(*) from term_aliases`). Its rows were inserted by the 057 baseline (`grep -c 'INSERT INTO "term_aliases"' scripts/migrations/057_baseline_2026-08-12.sql`), and the 2026-09-16 ruling retires data rows in place, never deleting them. A new `term_forms` beside it leaves those rows where they are forever: either copied (two homes) or reached through a union view (the matrix design's `v_base_lookup`), which is two homes joined at read time.
- **The matrix design's two objections are answered in place.** (i) "The PK has no jurisdiction or source": the rebuild replaces the PK by a surrogate key and an occurrence index that includes jurisdiction and locator (section 3). (ii) "It mixes model seeds with attested forms": T-026's typed `attestation` separates them in a cell, and every vocabulary read filters on it (section 8).
- **The name stays.** Renaming the table would make every caller a sweep item (`git grep -l -F term_aliases -- scripts schemas .github .claude skills ':(exclude)scripts/migrations'` and the prose `git grep` of the task file) for a legibility gain only; a row of `term_aliases` is documented as "a form of the concept, or a related search string" (section 5).

## 3. The table after T-026 and T-028 (sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: term_aliases after T-028's rebuild. Columns marked (T-026) are added by T-026 first.
CREATE TABLE term_aliases (
    form_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,   -- = the old rowid (pointers made by rowid still resolve)
    term_id             TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    alias               TEXT NOT NULL,                       -- the form, verbatim
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    alias_type          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (alias_type IN
                            ('SYNONYM','TRANSLATION','NARROWER','BROADER','DEPRECATED','DOMAIN')),  -- unchanged; section 5
    jurisdiction        TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    observation_id      INTEGER REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    attestation         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (attestation IN
                            ('instrument','other_source','owner_supplied','model_seed','unrecorded')),  -- (T-026)
    source_url          TEXT CHECK (source_url IS NULL OR source_url GLOB 'http*://*'),             -- (T-026)
    source_page         TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
    source_line         INTEGER CHECK (source_line IS NULL OR source_line > 0),                    -- (T-026)
    source_clause       TEXT,                                                                       -- (T-026)
    usage_type          TEXT CHECK (usage_type IS NULL OR usage_type IN
                            ('code_term','colloquial','regional_variant','outdated_or_disfavoured','product_name')),
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- (T-026) an attested occurrence says where; a seed says nowhere.
    CHECK (attestation NOT IN ('instrument','other_source')
           OR observation_id IS NOT NULL
           OR (source_url IS NOT NULL AND (source_page IS NOT NULL OR source_clause IS NOT NULL))),
    CHECK (attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')
           OR (source_url IS NULL AND source_page IS NULL AND source_line IS NULL AND source_clause IS NULL))
);
-- One row per OCCURRENCE: the same form in two sources or jurisdictions is two rows.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ux_term_aliases_occurrence ON term_aliases
    (term_id, alias, language, COALESCE(jurisdiction, ''), COALESCE(observation_id, 0),
     COALESCE(source_url, ''), COALESCE(source_clause, ''), COALESCE(source_page, ''),
     COALESCE(source_line, 0));
CREATE INDEX idx_ta_alias    ON term_aliases(alias);      -- recreated (exists today)
CREATE INDEX idx_ta_language ON term_aliases(language);   -- recreated (exists today)
```

`usage_type` is nullable: NULL means "not yet typed", which is the truth for every existing row; it is typed by judgment when a row is next touched (T-107), never guessed by the migration. The five values are the sixth statement's list, in the column's own CHECK (read by `dbcore.check_values`, never retyped).

## 4. What T-026 builds on this table (names fixed here; T-026 executes them)

- `attestation TEXT NOT NULL` with the five-value CHECK above (the sixth statement's four kinds plus `unrecorded`): `instrument` (a code, standard or statute uses the form), `other_source` (any other source uses it: signage manual, public-body or advocacy guidance, a study, a glossary), `owner_supplied` (a seed the owner gave), `model_seed` (a model generated it), `unrecorded` (no provenance). `instrument` and `other_source` are attestations; the other three are seeds or unknowns and are **search aids only** (E4).
- `source_url`, `source_page`, `source_line`, `source_clause`, and the two CHECKs of section 3.
- **Mechanical fill**, from what the row already says, with no judgment: `observation_id` set → `other_source` (an admitted source used the phrase; whether it is an instrument is a judgment left to T-107); notes carrying a `VERIFIED-GLOSSARY` or `VERIFIED-CROSS` marker → `other_source`; `model-generated` → `model_seed`; anything else, including `curated`, `repo shorthand`, `VERIFIED-NATIVE` and NULL notes → `unrecorded`. The markers are the ones `classify()` in `scripts/audit/alias_provenance_audit.py` reads; reuse that function's precedence. (The other_source rows carry no URL, so the first CHECK admits them through `observation_id` or, for the glossary markers, not at all: if `select count(*) from term_aliases where notes like '%VERIFIED-GLOSSARY%' or notes like '%VERIFIED-CROSS%'` is not 0 at execution, those rows go to `unrecorded` and are listed in T-026's pull request for T-107 to re-attest with a locator.)
- `add-alias` gains the base route of the seventh statement: `--source-url --source-page --source-line --source-clause --attestation instrument|other_source` as an alternative to `--observation-id`, and `--seed owner_supplied|model_seed` for a flagged seed with no locator.
- The search-forms junction (T-026 item 1) points at `term_aliases.form_id` once T-028 has run; until then at `rowid`, which T-028 preserves as `form_id`.

**Why the occurrence grain is T-028's and not T-026's:** T-026 adds columns by `ALTER TABLE` and needs no rebuild; the grain needs one. Until T-028 merges, a second occurrence of a form a term already holds in that language cannot be stored, so **T-107 (attest forms) now waits for T-028** (its task file is corrected in the same pass).

## 5. Membership, the legacy `alias_type` values, and conflation

- **Members of the equivalence class** are the rows whose `alias_type` is not `NARROWER` or `BROADER`. A `NARROWER` or `BROADER` row is a related search string, not a name of the concept: it is never shown as a name, never counted as a form, never matched as a name. (Term-to-term relations are T-029's table; these strings name no term.)
- **`TRANSLATION`, `DEPRECATED`, `DOMAIN` are legacy values.** Each joins a relation with another fact (a seed's origin; a usage; a domain variant). After T-026 and T-028 those facts have typed homes (`attestation`, `usage_type`). The existing rows are **not rewritten** (`DOMAIN` cannot be mapped to a usage without judgment: `select alias, language, notes from term_aliases where alias_type='DOMAIN'`); no writer writes these three values again; no reader infers attestation or usage from them. `add-alias` already refuses `TRANSLATION` and `DEPRECATED`; it now refuses `DOMAIN` too, naming `--usage-type`. `rename-term` stops writing `DEPRECATED` (section 8).
- **Conflation is derived, not stored:** a form held as a member by two concepts in one language is a conflation. Query: `select upper(language), alias, group_concat(distinct term_id) from term_aliases where alias_type not in ('NARROWER','BROADER') group by 1, 2 having count(distinct term_id) > 1`. Writers report it and do not refuse it when the operator names the other concept with `--distinct-from` (section 8).

## 6. `canonical_en`

- **Kept, `NOT NULL`, meaning "our English descriptive label".** Six committed data migrations INSERT `terms.canonical_en` (`git grep -l canonical_en -- 'scripts/migrations/data_*' | wc -l`) and six views read it as a parameter's name (`select name from sqlite_master where type='view' and sql like '%canonical_en%'`); every one keeps working because the column keeps its meaning: a label to show and to search our own registry by. Relaxing `NOT NULL` would rebuild `terms` for no gain once English labels are allowed (eighth statement).
- **Never a form.** No writer copies `canonical_en` into `term_aliases`. `rename-term` stops doing so (it wrote the old label as `DEPRECATED`); the former label stays recorded once, in the `scope_note` trailer `rename-term` already writes.
- **Marked as ours by derivation, not a column** (OD-03: "add no label-kind column"): `v_term_names.label_is_instrument_term` is 1 exactly when an attested member form of the same concept has the label's text. Otherwise the label is ours.
- **The 94 terms** (`select count(*) from terms`) are unchanged; every one derives `label_is_instrument_term = 0` today, because no row is attested yet (`select count(*) from term_aliases where observation_id is not null` prints 0, and T-026's fill adds no locator).
- The rule that a label must sit inside an observed phrase (the owner's 2026-09-09 rule, kept 2026-10-09) **still binds when the first form is English**; it is lifted only for a concept whose first form is not English, where the eighth statement allows an English descriptive label.

## 7. The name shown: `v_term_names` (E1 derived; sketch)

```sql
-- sketch: one view, the only reader of "what is this concept called"
CREATE VIEW v_term_names AS
WITH attested AS (                  -- member forms a source uses; seeds are never vocabulary (E4)
    SELECT form_id, term_id, alias, upper(language) AS language, jurisdiction, attestation
      FROM term_aliases
     WHERE alias_type NOT IN ('NARROWER','BROADER')
       AND attestation IN ('instrument','other_source')),
en_instrument AS (                  -- English forms an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses
    SELECT a.* FROM attested a
     WHERE a.attestation = 'instrument' AND a.language = 'EN'
       AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM v_research_scope r
                    WHERE upper(r.language) = 'EN' AND r.jurisdiction = a.jurisdiction)),
pick AS (
    SELECT t.term_id, t.canonical_en,
           (SELECT form_id FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id
              AND lower(e.alias) = lower(t.canonical_en) ORDER BY form_id LIMIT 1) AS en_label_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM en_instrument e WHERE e.term_id = t.term_id) AS en_first_form,
           (SELECT MIN(form_id) FROM attested o WHERE o.term_id = t.term_id
              AND o.attestation = 'instrument') AS origin_form
      FROM terms t)
SELECT p.term_id,
       p.canonical_en AS label,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM attested a WHERE a.term_id = p.term_id
                 AND lower(a.alias) = lower(p.canonical_en)) AS label_is_instrument_term,
       CASE WHEN p.en_label_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_label'
            WHEN p.en_first_form IS NOT NULL THEN 'english_instrument_form'
            WHEN p.origin_form   IS NOT NULL THEN 'origin_instrument_form'
            ELSE 'label_ours' END AS display_basis,
       COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form) AS display_form_id,
       COALESCE((SELECT alias FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                p.canonical_en) AS display_name,
       COALESCE((SELECT upper(language) FROM term_aliases f
                  WHERE f.form_id = COALESCE(p.en_label_form, p.en_first_form, p.origin_form)),
                'EN') AS display_language,
       p.origin_form AS origin_form_id
  FROM pick p;
```

**The rules, in order (E1, with the stored choice):**
1. Our label equals an English form an instrument of an owed English-language jurisdiction uses → show it (`english_instrument_label`). This is also how the stored, warranted choice works: `rename-term --from-form <form_id>` sets the label to one attested form (section 8).
2. Else an English instrument form of such a jurisdiction exists → show the first recorded of them (`english_instrument_form`). **Arbitrary when there are several** (for example two English-language codes naming one concept differently); the remedy is rule 1 via `rename-term`, and `select term_id from v_term_names v where display_basis='english_instrument_form' and (select count(distinct lower(alias)) from term_aliases a where a.term_id=v.term_id and upper(a.language)='EN' and a.attestation='instrument') > 1` lists the concepts owed that choice.
3. Else an instrument form in any language exists → show the origin instrument's phrase, in its own language (`origin_instrument_form`): E1 proper.
4. Else → show our label (`label_ours`), which a page marks as ours.

"Owed English-language jurisdiction" is read from `v_research_scope`, the one home of scope (T-101 fills it); no list of jurisdictions is typed. Readers: render (T-037, the name shown and the "ours" mark), any writer output that names a concept, the base coverage view when one is built (section 15).

## 8. Every writer that screens or matches a name, and how it changes

| Writer (locate by symbol in `scripts/db.py`) | Today | After T-028 |

| `_name_holder(conn, name, *, aliases, exclude_term)` | exact match on `canonical_en` first, then on any alias in any language | `_name_holder(conn, name, language, *, exclude_term=None)` returns **every** clash, none first: `label` (another term's `canonical_en`, case-folded, compared only when `language` is EN) and `form` (an **attested** member form in the same language, case-folded). Seeds never clash (E4); they are returned as `seed_matches` for information. |
| `_near_terms(conn, name)` | token overlap with every `canonical_en` and every EN alias | `_near_terms(conn, name, language)`: token overlap with attested member forms in `language`, and with labels only when `language` is EN. A non-English name is never screened against English. Tokenising is T-009's script-aware `_name_tokens`; until T-009 merges, a non-Latin name yields no tokens and no near match, which the refusal text must say. |

[--distinct-from TERM-ID ...] --session S`. Exactly one of `--from-observation` and `--first-form`. Writes the term and its first member row in one transaction. ## 9. Pointers to other homes

- **Translations (T-049).** A translation of a form is a `translations` row pointing at `('term_aliases', 'alias', <form_id>)`, never an alias and never a term; a concept is minted only from an observed or located phrase (no back-translation). # T-102 design — the mobility family decomposed by device

_Written 2026-11-12 by an Opus-class designer under the owner's instruction "Opus to write design files that must be written first". Plan document: it changes no script, schema, row or ruling, and it **decides no taxonomy**: every code, name and edge below is **PROPOSED (owner confirms)** through the report of section 10, which the T-102 executor appends to the ledger before any row is written. Every count is a command; re-run it. Canadian English._

## 0. Verdict

**Keep `MOB` as the active parent and add three children by device, each with `parent_code = 'MOB'`:**

| Code | Display name (PROPOSED) | Whom it names |
|---|---|---|
| `WHEEL` | wheelchair users | people who use a wheelchair for some or all of their mobility, ambulatory wheelchair users included |
| `PROSTH` | people who use a lower-limb prosthesis | people with lower-limb loss or difference who walk or stand with a prosthesis |
| `WALKAID` | people who use walking aids | people who walk with a cane or stick, crutches, a walking frame or a rollator |

`MOB` is renamed from "disabled people with mobility needs; wheelchair users" (two things in one cell) to **"disabled people with mobility needs"**. A provision that names no device stays on `MOB`; a person with a mobility need who uses no aid is reached through `MOB` and the ICF d4 codes and access needs, with no child. Wheelchair drive stays in `device_class` and never becomes a code; impairment level (paraplegia, quadriplegia) stays out of the identity lens (medical lens when a source names it, ICF b-codes for the function it changes). `device_class` gains three values: `lower_limb_prosthesis`, `crutches`, `cane`. Five edges are reported as open, each with a recommendation: the 2026-08-25 `AMB`, scooter users, ambulatory wheelchair users, the prosthesis code's overlap with `LMB`, and people with a mobility need who use no aid.

**Confidence.** High (about 85%) that the children should be device-defined with drive and level as descriptors: the owner's words, the memo's evidence (no retrieved organisation is constituted by drive or by level) and rule 5 agree. Medium (about 65%) on `WHEEL` including ambulatory wheelchair users and on scooter users staying on the parent. Medium (about 60%) on restricting the prosthesis child to lower-limb prostheses. Low to medium (about 50%) on the display names of `PROSTH` and `WALKAID`: no organisation of prosthesis users or of walking-aid users was retrieved (memo §3.3), so those names are descriptive, not self-chosen, and the report says so.
